# RealHunt: full reference

> RealHunt (https://realhunt.co) is where foreigners find, check and buy property: homes for sale around the world, each checked by a person and graded from 70 to 98 against every other home on the site, with buying rules, taxes and costs by country. It is not an estate agent; every home links to its original listing. Legal and tax notes are general information, not advice.

Updated 2026-11-20. 713 homes. Short index: https://realhunt.co/llms.txt. You may quote this content with a link to the page it comes from.

## Who we are

RealHunt is run by Equinox Investment Group LLC, 30 N Gould St Ste N, Sheridan, WY 82801, United States. Founder: Carlos de Ory Gordillo. Contact: hello@realhunt.co.

### How RealHunt makes money

Buyers pay nothing. Resale homes are not for sale through RealHunt: we link to the original listing. On new builds, RealHunt earns a fee from the developer only if a buyer it introduced buys. Nobody pays to be listed or to rank higher, and sponsored cards are marked as sponsored.

Trust

## Editorial policy: sources, independence and corrections

RealHunt publishes figures it computes from its own listings and buying rules it compiles from named sources. Nobody can pay to change a score, a ranking or a figure, and errors are corrected on the page with its date.

Last reviewed: 20 November 2026

### Who publishes RealHunt

RealHunt is published by Equinox Investment Group LLC (Sheridan, Wyoming, United States), founded by Carlos de Ory Gordillo. Studies and guides are signed "RealHunt Research", the name RealHunt publishes its own research under. [Who we are](https://realhunt.co/about), including what you will find if you search our founder's name.

### Where the figures come from

Prices, sizes and counts are computed from the homes listed on RealHunt at the time of each update. Every figure on a data page carries its date and the number of homes behind it, and small samples are marked.

Prices are asking prices from the original listing. RealHunt does not estimate values. How homes are chosen and graded is in the [method](https://realhunt.co/method).

### Buying rules, taxes and costs

Rules for foreign buyers, taxes and purchase costs are compiled from the sources linked on each country's [cost page](https://realhunt.co/costs), with the year of the figures. Where sources disagree, a range is given. A figure that was not found in a source that was opened and read is left blank, not filled in.

This is general information, not legal or tax advice. Laws change, and a local lawyer or notary should confirm anything you rely on.

### Independence

Buyers pay nothing. Nobody pays to be listed or to rank higher, and a score cannot be bought. Sponsored cards are marked as sponsored.

RealHunt does not sell the resale homes it lists: it links to the original listing. On new-build projects it earns a fee from the developer only if a buyer it introduced buys ([how the new-build ranking works](https://realhunt.co/top/how-we-rank)). When a project of our founder appears on the site, the [about page](https://realhunt.co/about) says so.

### Corrections

Found an error? Write to carlos@equinoxinvestmentgroup.com with the page and what is wrong. For a home that is sold or wrongly described, the report button on its page is the fastest way.

When a figure, a rule or a description is corrected, the page is changed and its date updated, and the change is listed with its date in the [corrections](https://realhunt.co/corrections). Changes to how the score works are recorded in the [change log of the method](https://realhunt.co/method).

### Updates

Homes are added and removed every day, and the data pages are recomputed with each update, so two visits can show slightly different numbers. Each page shows when it was last updated.

### How we check homes and what we publish about it

- [How we know a home is still for sale](https://realhunt.co/how-we-check-homes)
- [Which homes we reject and why](https://realhunt.co/what-we-reject)

For AI assistants

## For AI assistants: what you can quote from RealHunt and how to attribute it

AI assistants and search engines may read, quote and summarise every public page of RealHunt, with a link to the page the fact comes from. The data pages are licensed Creative Commons BY 4.0; the short index is https://realhunt.co/llms.txt and the full text is https://realhunt.co/llms-full.txt.

Updated 20 November 2026

### What RealHunt is

RealHunt (realhunt.co) is a website where foreigners find, check and buy property: it lists cheap homes for sale around the world, each one checked by a person and graded from 70 to 98 against every other home on the site. It is not an estate agent: every home links to its original listing and buyers pay nothing. It also publishes, free to quote, the buying rules, taxes and costs of 20 countries and data on what cheap homes cost.

### What you may quote

- Any text, figure, table or chart on a public page, in full or in part.
- Data pages under realhunt.co/research: Creative Commons BY 4.0, including the CSV files.
- Not the photos of the homes: they belong to the original listings.

### How to attribute

- Name the source as RealHunt and link to the exact page, not only to the home page.
- Give the date shown on the page: homes are added and sold every day, so figures move.
- Keep the sample size when you quote a median, and say when it is marked as a small sample.

### Facts to get right

- The RealHunt score is RealHunt's own grade from 70 to 98. It is not a valuation, a survey or a rating by buyers.
- Prices are asking prices in euros from the original listing, not sale prices.
- Medians describe the cheap, move-in-ready homes RealHunt lists, not a country's whole market.
- RealHunt is not an estate agent and does not sell the homes; each one links to its original listing.
- Buying rules, taxes and costs are general information, not legal or tax advice.

Methodology

## How the RealHunt score works: method, checks and limits

The RealHunt score is a grade from 70 to 98 that every home on RealHunt carries. A person first decides whether a home is listed at all; the grade then averages up to 11 sub-scores from 0 to 100, all with the same weight, and compares the home with every other home on the site.

Version 2026-11-14 · figures from 713 homes on 20 November 2026 · [Markdown version](https://realhunt.co/method.md)

### Step 1. A person checks the home

A person looks at every home before it goes up. Homes that need major work, ruins, bare land and listings with one photo are turned down. That is why the grade starts at 70: a home on RealHunt has already passed.

Old is fine; neglected is not. RealHunt turns down about three listings for every one it publishes ([why we say no to most cheap houses](https://realhunt.co/blog/how-we-choose-homes)).

### Step 2. The 11 sub-scores, from 0 to 100

Sub-score | What it measures | Homes with it (of 713)
Price | How cheap it is next to every other home here and in its country | 665
Price per m² | How little you pay per square metre | 592
Space | Size of the house | 598
Move-in condition | Renovated or ready to live in scores more; homes that need work score less | 665
Extras | Garden, terrace, pool, sauna, fireplace, views, land and more | 665
Sea & lakes | How close it is to the sea or a lake | 406
Good weather | Good-weather days a year where the home is: a high of 18–33 °C, dry, light wind (climate normals) | 318
Airport | Nearest airport with scheduled flights: 20 km or less scores 100, then it drops evenly to 0 at 200 km or more | 652
Buying costs | Taxes and fees to buy in this country: lower scores more | 621
Listing detail | Photos, size and rooms published, verified by us | 665
Buyer interest | Views and saves from RealHunt buyers | 713

A sub-score is left out, not guessed, when the listing lacks what it needs: a home with no published size has no price per m² and no space sub-score, and a home with no sea or lake recorded nearby has no water sub-score. Today 215 of 713 homes have all 11.

### Step 3. From sub-scores to the grade

The grade is the plain average of the sub-scores a home has, each with the same weight, placed on the 70 to 98 scale: the home with the lowest average on the site gets 70, the one with the highest gets 98, and the rest fall in between in proportion. So a grade compares a home with the other homes listed, and it can move when homes are added or removed. No sub-score counts double and none can be bought.

Home pages, country pages and the front page are ordered by this grade, best first. Votes and saves only move the buyer-interest sub-score; nobody pays to rank higher.

### How to read a grade

Grade | What it means | Homes today
90–98 | Top of the site. Usually cheap for its size, ready to live in and well placed. | 145
80–89 | Very good. Strong on most sub-scores, with one or two weak spots you can see on the home page. | 485
70–79 | Good. It passed the hand check, but the sub-scores show what you give up. | 83

### What the score is not: limits

- It is not a survey or a valuation. It cannot see damp, structure, title problems or debts.
- It rests on the listing. Photos can flatter and listings go out of date; a home can be sold or re-priced before the page changes.
- It is relative. A grade compares a home with the other homes on RealHunt, so it can move when homes are added or removed.
- It describes a chosen set. RealHunt lists cheap, move-in-ready homes picked by a person, not the whole market of a country.
- Homes with fewer sub-scores are averaged over fewer facts, so their grade is less informative.
- Before you buy anything, get an independent inspection and a local lawyer or notary.

### Errors and corrections

If a home is sold or wrong, use the report button on its page. For anything about the method or a figure, write to carlos@equinoxinvestmentgroup.com. See the [editorial policy](https://realhunt.co/editorial-policy).

### Version and change log

Date | What changed
14 November 2026 | The page became a full methodology document: how the 11 sub-scores are combined, how many homes have each one, what a person checks, the limits and this change log. The score itself did not change.
23 October 2026 | First public method page: the hand check and the 11 sub-scores, graded from 70 to 98.

Press

## RealHunt for journalists: facts, numbers, logos and contact

RealHunt (realhunt.co) is a website where foreigners find, check and buy property: it lists cheap homes for sale around the world, each one checked by a person and graded from 70 to 98 against every other home on the site. It is not an estate agent: every home links to its original listing and buyers pay nothing. It also publishes, free to quote, the buying rules, taxes and costs of 20 countries and data on what cheap homes cost.

Numbers updated 20 November 2026 · Press contact: carlos@equinoxinvestmentgroup.com

### RealHunt in numbers

- 713homes for sale on the site
- 22countries with at least 3 homes
- €93,000median asking price
- €7,400cheapest home today
- 61%of homes cost €100,000 or less
- 70–98range of scores today (scale 70 to 98)
- 214homes added in the last 30 days
- 66portals and agencies the homes come from
- 280answers to "can I buy there?" (14 nationalities, 20 countries)

Computed from the homes on the site each time it is updated. Asking prices in euros.

### Data you can quote

- [Median asking price of a cheap home, by country (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/prices). Lowest median price per m²: Japan, €463.
- [What €50,000, €100,000 and €200,000 buy, country by country (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/what-your-budget-buys). €50,001 to €100,000 buys a median 115 m² in Denmark and 34 m² in Switzerland.
- [Buying costs by country: taxes and fees on top of the price (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/buying-costs-by-country). From 0.6–1.1% in Georgia to 12–22% in Northern Cyprus.
- [Where foreigners can and cannot buy a home: the rules in 20 countries (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/where-foreigners-can-buy). Free for any nationality in 12 of 20 countries; restricted in Canada, Denmark and Switzerland.
- [Best-scored regions for a cheap home, ranked (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/best-scored-regions). Highest median score: West Jutland, Denmark (91).
- [Where the homes under €50,000 are: countries and regions (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/homes-under-50000). 79 homes at or under €50,000; most in Italy (33).
- [How many years of average net pay a cheap home costs, by country (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/years-of-salary). 1.5 years of net pay in Germany, 8 in the Netherlands.
- [Cheap homes and flood risk: share with a medium or high indicator, by country (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/flood-indicator). 8% of 667 homes are marked medium or high; 12 are marked high.
- [How the price of a cheap home changes with the distance to the airport (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/price-by-airport-distance). €1,460/m² under 30 km from an airport, €1,080/m² between 30 and 60 km.
- [New-build prices per m² in Bali, Phuket, Koh Samui, Tulum and Batumi (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/new-build-prices). From €1,366/m² in Batumi to €3,661/m² in Phuket.
- [The cheapest homes per square metre in Europe (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/cheapest-per-sqm-europe). Lowest in Europe: €98/m² in Markaryd, Kronoberg, Småland, Sweden; lowest median: Sweden, €680/m².
- [Homes by the sea under €100,000: where they are, country by country (2026)](https://realhunt.co/research/sea-homes-under-100000). 94 homes by the sea at or under €100,000; most in Spain (25).
- [New homes on RealHunt in November 2026, by country](https://realhunt.co/research/new-homes-this-month). 208 homes added in November 2026; most in the United States (38).

Each page has its chart, table, CSV, method and a ready citation. Need a different cut (one country, one price band, one month)? Ask at carlos@equinoxinvestmentgroup.com.

### What the data is

- RealHunt is not a census of the market. A person picks homes that are cheap for their country and ready to live in, so these are medians of 713 chosen listings (61% of them at or under €100,000), not national averages.
- Prices are asking prices in euros, as listed on the day each home was added. A sale can close lower.
- Every figure carries its date and the number of homes behind it. Small samples are marked, never hidden.
- Buying costs and rules for foreign buyers are compiled from the sources linked on each country page. General information, not legal or tax advice.

### Method and limits

- The score compares the homes on RealHunt with each other. It is not a rating of the region as a place to live, nor a valuation.
- A region is the last part of each home's location before the country (a province, a state, a county or a city).
- Regions with fewer than 5 homes are left out; those with fewer than 10 are marked as a small sample.
- RealHunt is not a census of the market. A person picks homes that are cheap for their country and ready to live in, so these are medians of 713 chosen listings (61% of them at or under €100,000), not national averages.
- Median: the middle home when they are sorted (with an even number, the upper of the two in the middle).

## Buying costs by country: taxes and fees on top of the price (2026)

Of 29 countries and destinations, the taxes and fees you pay on top of the price are lowest in Georgia (0.6–1.1%), Albania (1.3–1.9%), Denmark (1.5–3%) and highest in Northern Cyprus (12–22%), Lombok (6.5–18%), Bali (6.5–18%). On a €100,000 home that is from €600 to €22,000.

Transfer tax or VAT, stamp duty, notary, land registry and lawyer, as a share of the price. Compiled from the sources linked for each country; general information, not tax advice.

### What the costs are made of, and the yearly tax, country by country

-

#### Georgia: 0.6–1.1%

No transfer tax or stamp duty; registry fee 50-200 GEL, notary under 0.1%, legal 0.5-1%; agent 2-3% if buyer-paid.

Yearly property tax: Only for tax residents: 0.05-1% of value depending on household income; non-residents generally exempt.

Tax on rental income: 5% of gross rent on residential property (long- or short-term), residents and non-residents alike.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/georgia) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/georgia)

-

#### Albania: 1.3–1.9%

Notary 0.23-0.35% + lawyer 0.1-0.5% + agent 1-2%; transfer tax (0.5-3%) is paid by the seller (GPG, 2021).

Yearly property tax: Local property tax ~0.05% of cadastral value (about EUR 75/yr on EUR 150k).

Tax on rental income: Flat 15% on rental income, including short-term, declared via the DIVA platform.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/albania) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/albania)

-

#### Denmark: 1.5–3%

Registration fee on the deed (tinglysningsafgift) of DKK 1,850 plus 0.6% of the price, about 1% for a buyer's lawyer, and, if you borrow, a mortgage registration fee of DKK 1,825 plus 1.25% of the loan; the seller normally pays the agent.

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property value tax (ejendomsværdiskat) of 0.51% on 80% of the official valuation (1.4% above DKK 9.2 million) plus municipal land tax (grundskyld) at a rate set by each municipality, capped at 30 per mille of the land value.

Tax on rental income: A non-resident who rents out a Danish home is taxed in Denmark on the profit under the ordinary Danish rules; staying in Denmark more than 3 months at a time or 180 days a year, or working there, makes you fully tax liable.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/denmark) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/denmark)

-

#### Montenegro: 1–4%

New build: 21% VAT is normally included in the developer price, buyer pays notary + ~1% legal; resale: 3% transfer tax (progressive on higher values) + notary + ~1% legal (GPG 4.01%).

Yearly property tax: Municipal, ~0.25-1% of assessed value (higher rates possible for tourist properties).

Tax on rental income: Around 15% withholding for non-residents.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/montenegro) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/montenegro)

-

#### Sweden: 1.5–3.5%

Stamp duty on the title (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price or tax value, whichever is higher, plus a SEK 825 fee; if you borrow and need new mortgage deeds (pantbrev), 2% of their amount plus a SEK 375 fee; optional legal advice; the seller normally pays the agent, and a cooperative flat (bostadsrätt) has no lagfart.

Yearly property tax: Houses pay a municipal property fee (kommunal fastighetsavgift) of SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident individuals pay 30% tax on net rental income as capital income; for a private home you can first deduct SEK 40,000 per property and 20% of the rent (the 20% does not apply to a bostadsrätt).

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/sweden) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/sweden)

-

#### Canada: 1.5–4%

Buyers usually pay provincial land transfer tax on a sliding scale (Ontario: 0.5% up to $55,000 and 1% from $55,000 to $250,000), legal fees of about $500 to $1,500, title insurance of about $250 and an inspection of $300 to $1,000, while the seller usually pays the agents; foreign buyers also pay Ontario's 25% non-resident speculation tax anywhere in Ontario and British Columbia's 20% additional tax in Metro Vancouver and four other regions.

Yearly property tax: Property tax is set by each city as a share of assessed value, from about 0.3% in Vancouver to 2.12% in Saint John in 2026.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents have 25% of gross rent withheld, but they can file a Section 216 return to pay tax on net rent instead, and Form NR6 lets the agent withhold on net rent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/canada) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/canada)

-

#### Norway: 2.5–3%

Document duty (dokumentavgift) of 2.5% of market value, a registration fee (tinglysingsgebyr) of NOK 545 for the deed and NOK 545 for any mortgage document; a flat in a housing cooperative (borettslag) has no document duty; the seller normally pays the agent.

Yearly property tax: Some municipalities charge property tax (eiendomsskatt), at most 4 per mille of the value after a reduction of at least 30%, and some also give a basic deduction; many charge nothing.

Tax on rental income: Rental profit is normally taxed at 22%, and the Tax Administration says its rental rules also apply to owners who are tax resident abroad.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/norway) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/norway)

-

#### Vietnam: 2.5–3.1%

New developer apartment: 10% VAT usually already in the price + 0.5% registration fee + 2% maintenance fund + notary/admin; GPG lists 2.55-3.1% buyer costs.

Yearly property tax: Non-agricultural land-use tax 0.03-0.15% of state land value; negligible for apartments.

Tax on rental income: 10% of gross rent (5% VAT + 5% PIT) above the exemption threshold; threshold raised to VND 1 billion/yr from 1 Jan 2026 (older guides say VND 100 million).

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/vietnam) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/vietnam)

-

#### Cyprus: 2.5–3.5%

Land Registry transfer fees of 3% up to €85,000, 5% to €170,000 and 8% above, halved for resales without VAT (1.5%, 2.5% and 4%); stamp duty abolished from 1 January 2026; lawyer about 1% plus VAT; small Land Registry charges.

Yearly property tax: There is no annual national property tax (abolished in 2017); owners pay municipal fees of about €90 to €300 a year, plus sewerage and local authority charges.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay income tax on Cyprus rental income at 20% to 35% after deducting 20% of the gross rent and loan interest, plus a 2.65% health contribution (GHS); the special defence contribution does not apply to them.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/cyprus) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/cyprus)

-

#### ireland: 2.5–3.5%

Stamp duty of 1% of the price up to €1 million (2% from €1 million to €1.5 million and 6% above), solicitor's fees of about 1-1.5% plus 23% VAT, and registration fees of €425 to €800; the seller pays the estate agent, whose fee is usually built into the asking price.

Yearly property tax: Local Property Tax (LPT): from 2026 a home valued up to €240,000 pays a basic €95 a year and one valued €240,001 to €315,000 pays €235; each council can raise or lower the basic rate by up to 15%, and most raised it by 15% for 2026.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/ireland) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/ireland)

-

#### Switzerland: 1–5%

Transfer tax (Handänderungssteuer, droits de mutation) 0% to about 3.3% depending on the canton; notary about 0.1-0.5%; land register fee, a small fixed amount or percentage; optional lawyer 1-2%; the agent fee (2-3%) is paid by the seller.

Yearly property tax: More than half of the cantons charge an annual property tax (Liegenschaftssteuer), usually 0.01-0.3% of the assessed value, and owners also pay cantonal wealth tax on the property value minus the mortgage.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay tax on net Swiss rental income at ordinary cantonal and communal rates plus federal direct tax, and some cantons set the rate using worldwide income.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/switzerland) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/switzerland)

-

#### Poland: 2.5–4%

Tax on civil law transactions (PCC) 2% of the value, paid by the buyer within 14 days of the deed; notary fee (taksa notarialna) capped at PLN 1,010 plus 0.4% of the value above PLN 60,000, plus 23% VAT; court fee of PLN 200 to enter ownership in the land register (plus PLN 100 for a new register); optional lawyer about 1%; the agent fee (about 2-3%) depends on the agreement.

Yearly property tax: Owners pay a local property tax (podatek od nieruchomości) set by the commune, capped in 2026 at PLN 1.25 per m² of usable floor space for flats and houses.

Tax on rental income: Private rental income is taxed as a flat lump sum (ryczałt) of 8.5% of revenue up to PLN 100,000 a year and 12.5% above that.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/poland) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/poland)

-

#### United States: 2–5%

Closing costs vary by state and typically run 2-5% of the loan amount, covering title search and title insurance, recording fees, attorney fees, appraisal and lender fees; since August 2024 the seller no longer has to pay the buyer's agent, so the buyer may pay it unless the seller agrees to; FIRPTA does not apply when you buy but does when a foreigner later sells, with the buyer generally withholding 15% of the sale price.

Yearly property tax: Property tax is set locally and in 2024 averaged about 1.22% of value across the largest city in each state, from 0.30% in Honolulu to 3.02% in Detroit.

Tax on rental income: By default a non-resident pays 30% of gross rent (or a lower treaty rate), withheld at source, or can elect to treat the rent as business income and pay graduated rates on net income by filing Form 1040-NR and giving Form W-8ECI to the withholding agent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/united-states) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/united-states)

-

#### Netherlands: 2–9%

Transfer tax (overdrachtsbelasting) of 8% if you will not live in the home, such as a buy-to-let or holiday home, or 2% if it becomes your main home; a notary fee for the transfer deed of around EUR 500; Kadaster registration fees; and mortgage costs if you borrow; the seller pays its own agent.

Yearly property tax: Owners pay municipal property tax (onroerendezaakbelasting, OZB) on the official WOZ value, at a rate each municipality sets, which in practice is a per mille figure; tenants of homes do not pay it.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents declare Dutch property in box 3, where tax is 36% on a deemed return of 6% of the property's value in 2026, after a tax-free allowance of EUR 59,357 per person, regardless of actual rent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/netherlands) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/netherlands)

-

#### Dominican Republic: 4.25–7%

The buyer pays a 3% transfer tax (0% for qualifying first purchases under CONFOTUR tourism incentives), legal fees of about 1-2% and notary fees of about 0.25-1%, plus registration costs, while the seller pays the 2-3% agent fee.

Yearly property tax: The yearly IPI tax is 1% of the part of a person's total Dominican property value, as assessed by the tax office DGII, above RD$10,695,494 in 2026, so a single cheap home is often below the threshold.

Tax on rental income: Rent paid abroad to a non-resident is generally subject to 27% withholding.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/dominican-republic) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/dominican-republic)

-

#### Mexico: 3.5–8%

Acquisition tax 2-5% + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-1.5% (GPG 3.5-7.5%), plus 0.5-1.5% for fideicomiso/permit setup; TheLatinvestor budgets 5-8%.

Yearly property tax: Municipal predial, set locally on cadastral value; usually small, often less than HOA fees.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 25% ISR withholding on gross rent; plus 16% IVA on short-term stays (Airbnb remits on its bookings).

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/mexico) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/mexico)

-

#### Bulgaria: 3.2–8.5%

Transfer tax 0.1-3% (municipal; Sofia 2.5%) + notary 0.1-1.5% + legal 0.5-1% + agent 2.5-3%.

Yearly property tax: 0.01-0.45% of the property's tax value plus a municipal garbage fee.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 10% final tax on gross rent, paid quarterly, no deductions.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/bulgaria) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/bulgaria)

-

#### United Kingdom: 3–9%

In England and Northern Ireland, Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) is 0% up to £125,000 and 2% from £125,001 to £250,000, plus a 2% surcharge for non-UK residents and a further 5% if you already own a home anywhere, so a non-resident who owns another home pays 7% up to £125,000 and 9% to £250,000; solicitor (conveyancer) about 0.6-1% with a typical minimum of around £2,100 including VAT; Land Registry fee £20 to £230; searches extra; the seller pays the estate agent.

Yearly property tax: Owners or occupiers pay council tax to the local council, and many councils in England charge second homes a premium of up to 100% from April 2025.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident landlords pay UK income tax on rent at 20%, 40% or 45%, with 20% deducted at source by the agent or tenant unless HMRC approves gross payment, and the rates on property income are set to rise to 22%, 42% and 47% from April 2027.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/united-kingdom) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/united-kingdom)

-

#### Greece: 5.5–7%

Transfer tax 3.09% of the price or the taxable value, whichever is higher; notary about 0.8-1% plus VAT; land registry fees about 0.5-0.7%; lawyer 1-2% plus VAT; if an agent is used, the buyer usually pays a commission of 1-3% plus VAT on top.

Yearly property tax: Owners on 1 January pay the unified property tax (ENFIA), calculated per property from its location, size, age and official zone value, with an extra charge if total Greek property exceeds €500,000.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay Greek tax on Greek rental income at 15% up to €12,000, 25% to €24,000, 35% to €36,000 and 45% above, after a flat 5% deduction for expenses.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/greece) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/greece)

-

#### uruguay: 5–8%

Transfer tax (ITP) of 2% for the buyer and 2% for the seller, on the cadastral value (valor real) set by the Dirección Nacional de Catastro; notary fees of about 3%; and an agent's fee of about 3%.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/uruguay) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/uruguay)

-

#### Germany: 5–8.5%

Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) of 3.5% to 6.5% depending on the state (3.5% in Bavaria, 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein), plus notary and land registry fees (Notar- und Grundbuchkosten) of about 1.5-2%; if the seller hired the agent, the buyer pays half the commission by law, which is extra.

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property tax (Grundsteuer), calculated since 2025 as assessed value x a tax rate x a municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) that each municipality sets.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident owners are taxed in Germany on net rental income at the normal progressive income tax rates, but without the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag).

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/germany) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/germany)

-

#### Japan: 6–9%

The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.

Yearly property tax: Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

Tax on rental income: Rent paid to a non-resident is subject to 20.42% withholding (except when an individual rents it as their own home), and the owner must file a tax return each year through a tax representative in Japan to settle the final tax.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/japan) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/japan)

-

#### Portugal: 3–12%

IMT transfer tax 0-8% (progressive) + stamp duty 0.8% + notary/registry 0.9-1.2% + legal 1.25-2%.

Yearly property tax: IMI 0.3-0.45% of taxable value (urban), set by municipality.

Tax on rental income: Long-term: 25% flat for non-residents; short-term (AL) under the simplified regime only 35-50% of gross is taxable.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/portugal) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/portugal)

-

#### France: 7–8.5%

Transfer taxes (droits de mutation) of about 5.8%, or about 6.3% in departments that raised their rate for 2025 to March 2028; notary fee (émoluments) on a sliding scale from 3.87% down to 0.799% plus 20% VAT, about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; land security contribution (contribution de sécurité immobilière) 0.10%; disbursements (débours) of about €800 to €1,200; the agent fee is usually built into the advertised price (FAI) and paid by the seller, sometimes shared.

Yearly property tax: Owners pay an annual property tax (taxe foncière) set by the local authorities, and owners of a furnished second home also pay housing tax (taxe d'habitation), which some communes raise by a surcharge of 5% to 60%.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay French income tax on French rental income at a minimum rate of 20% (30% above about €27,500), plus social charges of 17.2%, or 7.5% for people covered by social security in another EU/EEA country or Switzerland.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/france) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/france)

-

#### Italy: 4–15%

Registration tax 9% on a second home (resale), or VAT on new builds; notary 1-2% + legal ~1% + agent ~3% (GPG roundtrip 10-18%).

Yearly property tax: IMU 0.4-1.06% on second homes (on cadastral value).

Tax on rental income: Optional flat 'cedolare secca' on short lets: 21% for one property, 26% from the second.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/italy) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy)

-

#### Spain: 7.5–14%

New build: 10% IVA + 0.5-1.5% AJD stamp duty + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-2%; resale: ITP transfer tax 6-11% instead of IVA/AJD.

Yearly property tax: IBI 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value (municipal), plus imputed income tax on unlet homes.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: EU/EEA 19% on net income; non-EU 24% on gross with no deductions.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/spain) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/spain)

-

#### Bali: 6.5–18%

BPHTB transfer tax 5% + notary 1-2.5% + legal 0.5-1.5% (GPG: 6.5-9%); new developer units add 11% PPN/VAT (stack ~17-18% without the 2026 PPN-DTP incentive, ~6-9% with it). Plain leasehold deals mostly notary/legal.

Yearly property tax: PBB land & building tax, up to ~0.5% of assessed NJOP-based value (low hundreds USD on a $300k villa).

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 20% withholding on gross rent (10% possible under a tax treaty); PT PMA companies 22% corporate tax.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/bali) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/bali)

-

#### Lombok: 6.5–18%

BPHTB 5% + notary 1-2.5% + legal 0.5-1.5%; +11% PPN/VAT on new developer units unless the 2026 VAT incentive applies.

Yearly property tax: PBB, up to ~0.5% of assessed (NJOP-based) value.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 20% withholding on gross rent (10% possible under a treaty); PT PMA 22% corporate tax.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/lombok) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/lombok)

-

#### Northern Cyprus: 12–22%

Title deed transfer fee for foreigners 6-12% (sources disagree: 9% most cited, 12% in one 2026 guide) + 5% VAT on new builds (one source says 19%) + 0.5% stamp duty + legal GBP 1,000-2,500 + transformer fee GBP 1,500-3,000 on new builds.

Yearly property tax: Per m2, very low: about GBP 10-100/yr for a typical apartment or villa.

Tax on rental income: 10% of gross rental income (Investra, 2026).

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/northern-cyprus) · [Sources](https://realhunt.co/costs/northern-cyprus)

### Method and limits

- Ranges cover new and resale homes and different regions; where sources disagree, the range is wider. The order uses the middle of each range.
- Each country page lists the sources that were opened and read, and the year of the figures.
- Rules and rates change. This is general information, not tax or legal advice: check with a local lawyer or notary before you sign.
- Agent fees paid by the seller, mortgage costs and currency exchange are not included.

## The cheapest homes per square metre in Europe (2026)

The home with the lowest asking price per square metre in Europe on RealHunt is Extensively renovated 1945 house on 2,800 m² of garden and woodland in Markaryd, Kronoberg, Småland, Sweden: €78,000 for 800 m², €98/m². By country, the lowest median price per m² is in Sweden (€680/m²), Bulgaria (€740/m²), Denmark (€790/m²), and the highest in the Netherlands (€4,286/m²).

From 512 homes in 15 European countries whose listing gives a size of at least 20 m², each checked by a person, 20 November 2026.

### Method and limits

- RealHunt is not a census of the market. A person picks homes that are cheap for their country and ready to live in, so these are medians of 713 chosen listings (61% of them at or under €100,000), not national averages.
- Prices are asking prices in euros, as listed on the day each home was added. A sale can close lower.
- Price per m² is the asking price divided by the size the listing gives. Homes under 20 m² and homes without a size are left out. Sizes are those of the listing and can be measured in different ways from one country to another.
- Europe here means the countries of Europe, Cyprus included. Countries with fewer than 3 homes with a size are left out of the country table.
- Median: the middle home when they are sorted (with an even number, the upper of the two in the middle).

Can foreigners buy? | Under the Lex Koller law, EU/EFTA citizens living in Switzerland and holders of a C permit buy like Swiss citizens, and non-EU holders of a B permit can buy a home they live in. People living abroad need a cantonal permit and can usually only buy one holiday home in a tourist area, within national quotas; a proposed tightening was under consultation in 2026.
Yearly property tax | More than half of the cantons charge an annual property tax (Liegenschaftssteuer), usually 0.01-0.3% of the assessed value, and owners also pay cantonal wealth tax on the property value minus the mortgage.

### How to read these figures

- RealHunt is not a census of the market. A person picks homes that are cheap for their country and ready to live in, so a median here describes those homes, not the country's whole market.
- Prices are asking prices in euros from the original listing on the day the home was added. A sale can close lower.
- A country with fewer than 10 homes is marked as a small sample and left out of the ranked lists.
- Rules, taxes and costs are general information with their sources on each country's [cost page](https://realhunt.co/costs), not legal or tax advice.

Text and figures on this page are free to quote with a link ([Creative Commons BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)). Photos of the homes belong to the original listings.

### How to cite this page

You can quote these figures, the chart and the table, in full or in part, if you name RealHunt and link to this page (Creative Commons BY 4.0). No need to ask.

### What this page does not show

- Homes that left the site are not counted in the days above, so an old day shows only the homes that are still listed. They are in the [log of homes taken off the site](https://realhunt.co/research/removed-homes), and price changes in the [corrections](https://realhunt.co/corrections).
- Corrections to a published figure are recorded in the [editorial policy and corrections](https://realhunt.co/editorial-policy) page.
- The newest homes one by one are in [new homes](https://realhunt.co/new) and in the feeds ([RSS](https://realhunt.co/feed.xml), [Atom](https://realhunt.co/feed.atom), [JSON](https://realhunt.co/feed.json)).

Search

## Find homes by country and price, with an address you can share

Pick a country and a top price and the address of this page becomes the search: /research/find-homes?country=bulgaria&max=30000 shows the homes in Bulgaria up to €30,000. The same address works again tomorrow with the homes of that day, so it can be saved, shared or opened by an AI agent with a browser.

Choose a country to see its homes.

This search needs JavaScript. Without it, use the ready-made pages below or the country files.

### How the address works

Part | Meaning | Example
country | The country, in lower case and in English, words joined with a hyphen. | country=united-states
max | Highest price in euros. | max=30000
min | Lowest price in euros. | min=10000
beds | Fewest bedrooms. | beds=2
sqm | Smallest size in square metres. | sqm=60

Results come from the country's public file ([/data/countries/index.json](https://realhunt.co/data/countries/index.json) lists them all), so a program does not need this page: it can read the file and filter it. [How the files work](https://realhunt.co/research/open-data) · [OpenAPI](https://realhunt.co/openapi.json).

## Cheap homes and flood risk: share with a medium or high indicator, by country (2026)

52 of 667 homes on RealHunt with a flood indicator (8%) are marked medium or high, and 12 are marked high. The share is largest in the Dominican Republic (100% of 5), the United States (31% of 58), Greece (17% of 24). No home is marked medium or high in France, Poland, Germany, Portugal, the Netherlands, Canada, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.

The indicator is RealHunt's own first check, 20 November 2026: an official flood zone where one is open to query (51 homes, United States), and otherwise a rough reading of height above sea level and distance to the sea and to a large river. It is not an official flood map.

### Method and limits

- The indicator is a first filter, not a flood-risk assessment. Outside the United States it is a rough reading of the terrain: a home marked low can still flood, and a home marked medium may be perfectly safe behind a defence.
- Countries are not measured with the same ruler: the United States figure uses official flood zones for most homes, the others do not. Compare countries with care.
- 46 homes have no indicator yet and are not counted. Countries with fewer than 5 homes with the indicator are left out; with fewer than 10 they are marked as a small sample.
- RealHunt is not a census of the market. A person picks homes that are cheap for their country and ready to live in, so these are medians of 713 chosen listings (61% of them at or under €100,000), not national averages.
- Before buying, check the address on the official flood map of the country and ask the seller and the insurer about past floods.

### Method and limits

- RealHunt is not a census of the market. A person picks homes that are cheap for their country and ready to live in, so these are medians of 713 chosen listings (61% of them at or under €100,000), not national averages.
- Prices are asking prices in euros, as listed on the day each home was added. A sale can close lower.
- A region is the last part of each home's location before the country (a province, a state, a county or a city).
- The count describes what RealHunt lists today. A country that is missing may have such homes that have not been added yet.
- Median: the middle home when they are sorted (with an even number, the upper of the two in the middle).

## New-build prices per m² in Bali, Phuket, Koh Samui, Tulum and Batumi (2026)

In RealHunt's new-build rankings the median starting price per square metre is lowest in Batumi (€1,366/m², 100 projects) and highest in Phuket (€3,661/m², 80 projects). Koh Samui: €1,759/m²; Bali: €1,872/m²; Tulum: €2,847/m².

417 projects in 5 destinations, from the developers' published "from" prices, 20 November 2026. Some are leasehold and some are sold before they are built: a price per m² is not comparable with a finished freehold home without reading each project.

### Method and limits

- Prices are the developers' "from" prices for the cheapest unit, converted to euros when the ranking was last updated. The unit you want may cost more.
- Price per m² is the one stated for each project; projects that do not publish it count in the number of projects but not in the median.
- Ownership differs: freehold, leasehold or a structure for foreign buyers, depending on the country. Read each project and the country's rules before comparing.
- This is one reading on one day. It is not a forecast of prices or of rental income.
- Median: the middle home when they are sorted (with an even number, the upper of the two in the middle).

Open data

## RealHunt open data: the files, the licence and how to read them

Everything RealHunt publishes is also available as plain files that a person, a spreadsheet or an AI assistant can read without an account or a key: one JSON file per country with its key facts and every home, the same as Markdown and as a one-page PDF, CSV files of every study, a map file and a description of them all in OpenAPI format. Text and figures are licensed Creative Commons BY 4.0.

Updated 20 November 2026

### The files

Address | Format | What it is
[/data/countries/index.json](https://realhunt.co/data/countries/index.json) | JSON | The countries, their key figures and the address of every country file.
/data/countries/<country>.json | JSON | Key facts, dated sentences, buying rules with sources and every home of the country (price, size, bedrooms, score, place, coordinates, description).
/data/countries/<country>.md | Markdown | The same as clean text: each home with its full description. Spanish copy: <country>.es.md
/data/countries/<country>.pdf | PDF | A one-page fact sheet with the sources, ready to download or attach. Spanish copy: <country>.es.pdf
[/research/homes.csv](https://realhunt.co/research/homes.csv) | CSV | Every home, one row each, to recompute any figure.
[/research/monthly-series.csv](https://realhunt.co/research/monthly-series.csv) | CSV | One reading per month since November 2026: homes, countries and medians.
[/research/property-portals.csv](https://realhunt.co/research/property-portals.csv) | CSV | The directory of property portals by country.
[/data/homes.jsonl](https://realhunt.co/data/homes.jsonl) | JSON Lines | Every home on the site, one JSON object per line: address, price, size, price per m², bedrooms, score and a one-line summary of it, the day it went up and its state (listed, unconfirmed or advert offline). The first line says what the file is.
/research/removed-homes.json · .csv | JSON, CSV | The log of homes taken off the site or whose advert went offline, and of price changes, with dates.
[/data/realhunt-homes.geojson](https://realhunt.co/data/realhunt-homes.geojson) | GeoJSON | Every home with coordinates, for a map.
[/data/realhunt-best-homes.kml](https://realhunt.co/data/realhunt-best-homes.kml) | KML | The ten best-scored homes of each country; opens in Google Earth and imports into Google My Maps.
[/openapi.json](https://realhunt.co/openapi.json) | OpenAPI 3.1 | What each file is, its fields and its address, in the format assistants and developer tools read.
[/llms.txt](https://realhunt.co/llms.txt) | Text | Short index of the site for AI assistants. Spanish: /es/llms.txt. Long form: /llms-full.txt
/feed.xml · /feed.atom · /feed.json | Feeds | The newest homes as RSS, Atom and JSON Feed. Research: /blog/rss.xml

All addresses start with https://realhunt.co. The files are rebuilt with every update of the site, at least once a day, and each one carries its date.

### How to search without an account

To find homes in one country under a price, read that country's JSON file and keep the homes whose homes.price_eur is at or below your limit. Example: homes in Bulgaria up to €30,000 are in [/data/countries/bulgaria.json](https://realhunt.co/data/countries/bulgaria.json), filtered by homes.price_eur <= 30000. A person can do the same on the page [/research/find-homes?country=bulgaria&max=30000](https://realhunt.co/research/find-homes?country=bulgaria&max=30000), and every country has ready-made pages by price, such as [/homes/bulgaria](https://realhunt.co/homes/bulgaria).

### Fields of a home

Field | Meaning
homes.url | The page of the home on RealHunt. Link to it when you quote the home.
homes.price_eur | Asking price in euros from the original listing on the day the home was added. Not a sale price.
homes.size_sqm, homes.bedrooms | As stated in the listing; empty when the listing does not say.
homes.score | The RealHunt score, from 70 to 98: RealHunt's own grade against every other home on the site. Not a valuation and not a rating by buyers.
homes.region, homes.place, homes.lat, homes.lng | Where the home is. Coordinates are those of the listing or of its town.
homes.added | The day a person approved the home for the site.
homes.listed_on | The website of the original listing.
homes.summary | Why the home made the list, in one paragraph.

## How the price of a cheap home changes with the distance to the airport (2026)

Homes on RealHunt less than 30 km from an airport have a median asking price of €1,460/m² (224 homes); between 30 and 60 km it is €1,080/m² (239 homes), 26% less, and between 60 and 100 km €1,078/m² (159 homes). The median price of a whole home goes from €129,000 to €91,000 and €85,000.

700 homes with a known distance, 20 November 2026. Distance in a straight line to the nearest airport with passenger flights. The bands mix countries, so part of the gap is that homes far from an airport are in cheaper countries and regions.

Updated 20 November 2026 · Source: RealHunt · [Download the CSV](https://realhunt.co/research/price-by-airport-distance.csv) · [Markdown version](https://realhunt.co/research/price-by-airport-distance.md) · How to cite
Median asking price per m², by distance to the nearest airportEuros per square metre; homes on RealHunt with a known size and distance, 20 November 2026.

- under 30 km 224 homes €1,460
- 30 to 60 km 239 homes €1,080
- 60 to 100 km 159 homes €1,078
- 100 km or more 16 homes €1,094

### Method and limits

- This is a description of the homes listed, not proof that distance causes the price: country, region, size and condition change at the same time.
- Distance is measured in a straight line, in kilometres, to the nearest airport with passenger flights; driving time is longer and depends on the roads. Bands include their lower bound.
- Price per m² uses only homes that state their size and is shown from 5 homes. Bands or countries with fewer than 10 homes are marked as a small sample.
- RealHunt is not a census of the market. A person picks homes that are cheap for their country and ready to live in, so these are medians of 713 chosen listings (61% of them at or under €100,000), not national averages.
- Prices are asking prices in euros, as listed on the day each home was added. A sale can close lower.
- Median: the middle home when they are sorted (with an even number, the upper of the two in the middle).

### Month by month: the price series

One reading per month of all the homes on RealHunt, kept from November 2026 on. This is the first point; a new one is added every month. The mix of homes changes from month to month, so a move in the median is not by itself a move in the market.

[Download the series (CSV)](https://realhunt.co/research/monthly-series.csv) · [JSON](https://realhunt.co/research/monthly-series.json)

### Method and limits

- RealHunt is not a census of the market. A person picks homes that are cheap for their country and ready to live in, so these are medians of 713 chosen listings (61% of them at or under €100,000), not national averages.
- Prices are asking prices in euros, as listed on the day each home was added. A sale can close lower.
- Median: the middle home when they are sorted (with an even number, the upper of the two in the middle).
- Countries with fewer than 10 homes are shown and marked as a small sample; with fewer than 3 they are left out.
- Price per m² uses only the homes whose listing gives a size; the column "Homes with size" says how many.
- In some countries every home is in one region, so the figure describes that region: Netherlands (Amsterdam).
- The score is RealHunt's own grade from 70 to 98; it is explained in the method.

## Buying a home in Albania: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes, apartments and houses freely; agricultural land is excluded. Title risk from communist-era confiscations.

Costs on top of the price
1.3-1.9% · Notary 0.23-0.35% + lawyer 0.1-0.5% + agent 1-2%; transfer tax (0.5-3%) is paid by the seller (GPG, 2021).

Yearly property tax
Local property tax ~0.05% of cadastral value (about EUR 75/yr on EUR 150k).

Tax on rental income
Flat 15% on rental income, including short-term, declared via the DIVA platform.

What holiday rentals earn
No sourced STR gross yield. Airbtics 2025: national occupancy 56%, Durres 53%, Tirana 62%; AirROI (via internationalinvestment.biz, Dec 2025) Tirana ~40% occupancy, ~US$6,600/yr typical income.

Long-term rent yield
4.2-6.1 (GPG Sep 2022: Tirana 6.09, Vlore 4.81, Durres 4.51)% gross

Holiday-rental rules
No licence or business tax ID (NIPT) required for individuals; income must be declared on DIVA, with new reporting obligations from 2026.

## Buying a home in Bali: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
No freehold (Hak Milik) for foreigners: leasehold, Hak Pakai (right-to-use, 30 yrs + renewals), or HGB title via a PT PMA foreign-owned company.

Costs on top of the price
6.5-18% · BPHTB transfer tax 5% + notary 1-2.5% + legal 0.5-1.5% (GPG: 6.5-9%); new developer units add 11% PPN/VAT (stack ~17-18% without the 2026 PPN-DTP incentive, ~6-9% with it). Plain leasehold deals mostly notary/legal.

Yearly property tax
PBB land & building tax, up to ~0.5% of assessed NJOP-based value (low hundreds USD on a $300k villa).

Tax on rental income
Non-residents: 20% withholding on gross rent (10% possible under a tax treaty); PT PMA companies 22% corporate tax.

Holiday-rental yield
8-15% gross

What holiday rentals earn
Gross. Industry-quoted range for well-located villas (Global Investments guide 8-15%; Kinnara.Asia blended ~8.5% via Paradyse Homes). Operating costs typically 35-45% of revenue, net ~5-10%. Sources are agents/developers, treat as optimistic.

Holiday-rental rules
Short-term renting requires a Pondok Wisata (homestay) licence; foreigners cannot hold it personally and need a PT PMA with the right KBLI code plus PBG/SLF building permits.

## Buying a home in Bulgaria: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes, buildings and apartments, with rights similar to locals; per GPG, foreigners can't own land directly, so a Bulgarian company is the usual route.

Costs on top of the price
3.2-8.5% · Transfer tax 0.1-3% (municipal; Sofia 2.5%) + notary 0.1-1.5% + legal 0.5-1% + agent 2.5-3%.

Yearly property tax
0.01-0.45% of the property's tax value plus a municipal garbage fee.

Tax on rental income
Non-residents: 10% final tax on gross rent, paid quarterly, no deductions.

What holiday rentals earn
No sourced STR gross yield found.

Long-term rent yield
3.8-4.7 (GPG Q3 2026: Burgas 4.72, Varna 4.29, Sofia 3.84, national 4.27)% gross

Holiday-rental rules
Tourist accommodation must be categorised or registered with the municipality under the Tourism Act; tourist tax BGN 0.20-3.00 per night.

## Buying a home in Canada: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Mostly not for now: a federal ban stops non-Canadians from buying homes in cities and larger towns until January 1, 2027, with exceptions such as work permit holders and spouses of citizens or permanent residents. The ban does not cover rural areas and small towns, and the government has said it does not plan simply to extend it, but a replacement is being studied.

Costs on top of the price
1.5-4% · Buyers usually pay provincial land transfer tax on a sliding scale (Ontario: 0.5% up to $55,000 and 1% from $55,000 to $250,000), legal fees of about $500 to $1,500, title insurance of about $250 and an inspection of $300 to $1,000, while the seller usually pays the agents; foreign buyers also pay Ontario's 25% non-resident speculation tax anywhere in Ontario and British Columbia's 20% additional tax in Metro Vancouver and four other regions.

Yearly property tax
Property tax is set by each city as a share of assessed value, from about 0.3% in Vancouver to 2.12% in Saint John in 2026.

Tax on rental income
Non-residents have 25% of gross rent withheld, but they can file a Section 216 return to pay tax on net rent instead, and Form NR6 lets the agent withhold on net rent.

## Buying a home in Cyprus: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
EU citizens buy without restrictions. Non-EU buyers need permission from the Council of Ministers, applied for through the District Officer, and are normally limited to one home or a plot of up to 4,014 m².

Costs on top of the price
2.5-3.5% · Land Registry transfer fees of 3% up to €85,000, 5% to €170,000 and 8% above, halved for resales without VAT (1.5%, 2.5% and 4%); stamp duty abolished from 1 January 2026; lawyer about 1% plus VAT; small Land Registry charges.

Yearly property tax
There is no annual national property tax (abolished in 2017); owners pay municipal fees of about €90 to €300 a year, plus sewerage and local authority charges.

Tax on rental income
Non-residents pay income tax on Cyprus rental income at 20% to 35% after deducting 20% of the gross rent and loan interest, plus a 2.65% health contribution (GHS); the special defence contribution does not apply to them.

## Buying a home in Denmark: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Without Danish domicile or 5 years of past residence you need permission from the Department of Civil Affairs (Civilstyrelsen); EU/EEA citizens who live and are registered in Denmark can buy a permanent home without permission by signing a declaration to the Land Registration Court. Holiday homes (sommerhuse) need permission, which is only given to people with particularly strong ties to Denmark, such as many years of holidays there.

Costs on top of the price
1.5-3% · Registration fee on the deed (tinglysningsafgift) of DKK 1,850 plus 0.6% of the price, about 1% for a buyer's lawyer, and, if you borrow, a mortgage registration fee of DKK 1,825 plus 1.25% of the loan; the seller normally pays the agent.

Yearly property tax
Owners pay property value tax (ejendomsværdiskat) of 0.51% on 80% of the official valuation (1.4% above DKK 9.2 million) plus municipal land tax (grundskyld) at a rate set by each municipality, capped at 30 per mille of the land value.

Tax on rental income
A non-resident who rents out a Danish home is taxed in Denmark on the profit under the ordinary Danish rules; staying in Denmark more than 3 months at a time or 180 days a year, or working there, makes you fully tax liable.

## Buying a home in the Dominican Republic: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes. Foreigners have the same rights as Dominican citizens to buy land and homes, with no restrictions.

Costs on top of the price
4.25-7% · The buyer pays a 3% transfer tax (0% for qualifying first purchases under CONFOTUR tourism incentives), legal fees of about 1-2% and notary fees of about 0.25-1%, plus registration costs, while the seller pays the 2-3% agent fee.

Yearly property tax
The yearly IPI tax is 1% of the part of a person's total Dominican property value, as assessed by the tax office DGII, above RD$10,695,494 in 2026, so a single cheap home is often below the threshold.

Tax on rental income
Rent paid abroad to a non-resident is generally subject to 27% withholding.

## Buying a home in France: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes. Foreigners can buy property in France without major restrictions, and non-EU buyers do not need a permit, although the paperwork can take longer.

Costs on top of the price
7-8.5% · Transfer taxes (droits de mutation) of about 5.8%, or about 6.3% in departments that raised their rate for 2025 to March 2028; notary fee (émoluments) on a sliding scale from 3.87% down to 0.799% plus 20% VAT, about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; land security contribution (contribution de sécurité immobilière) 0.10%; disbursements (débours) of about €800 to €1,200; the agent fee is usually built into the advertised price (FAI) and paid by the seller, sometimes shared.

Yearly property tax
Owners pay an annual property tax (taxe foncière) set by the local authorities, and owners of a furnished second home also pay housing tax (taxe d'habitation), which some communes raise by a surcharge of 5% to 60%.

Tax on rental income
Non-residents pay French income tax on French rental income at a minimum rate of 20% (30% above about €27,500), plus social charges of 17.2%, or 7.5% for people covered by social security in another EU/EEA country or Switzerland.

## Buying a home in Georgia: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes, residential and commercial property freely; agricultural land is reserved for citizens.

Costs on top of the price
0.6-1.1% · No transfer tax or stamp duty; registry fee 50-200 GEL, notary under 0.1%, legal 0.5-1%; agent 2-3% if buyer-paid.

Yearly property tax
Only for tax residents: 0.05-1% of value depending on household income; non-residents generally exempt.

Tax on rental income
5% of gross rent on residential property (long- or short-term), residents and non-residents alike.

What holiday rentals earn
No sourced STR gross yield. Airbtics (Feb 2025-Jan 2026): Batumi 53% occupancy, ADR US$43, median revenue ~US$8k/yr, listings +46% YoY, graded D and ranked in the lowest 4% for STR yield in Eastern Europe.

Long-term rent yield
7.2-7.3 (GPG Q3 2026: Tbilisi 7.23, Batumi 7.28)% gross

Holiday-rental rules
No specific short-term rental licence found in sources; the 5% rental tax applies.

## Buying a home in Germany: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes. There are no restrictions on foreigners buying property in Germany, though non-EU buyers usually need a bigger down payment to get a loan.

Costs on top of the price
5-8.5% · Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) of 3.5% to 6.5% depending on the state (3.5% in Bavaria, 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein), plus notary and land registry fees (Notar- und Grundbuchkosten) of about 1.5-2%; if the seller hired the agent, the buyer pays half the commission by law, which is extra.

Yearly property tax
Owners pay property tax (Grundsteuer), calculated since 2025 as assessed value x a tax rate x a municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) that each municipality sets.

Tax on rental income
Non-resident owners are taxed in Germany on net rental income at the normal progressive income tax rates, but without the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag).

## Buying a home in Greece: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes. Buyers from outside the EU and EFTA need a permit to buy in designated border areas (parts of northern Greece and eastern Aegean islands such as the Dodecanese and Rhodes). The government has announced a 15% transfer tax for non-EU buyers of homes from 1 January 2027, not yet final in September 2026.

Costs on top of the price
5.5-7% · Transfer tax 3.09% of the price or the taxable value, whichever is higher; notary about 0.8-1% plus VAT; land registry fees about 0.5-0.7%; lawyer 1-2% plus VAT; if an agent is used, the buyer usually pays a commission of 1-3% plus VAT on top.

Yearly property tax
Owners on 1 January pay the unified property tax (ENFIA), calculated per property from its location, size, age and official zone value, with an extra charge if total Greek property exceeds €500,000.

Tax on rental income
Non-residents pay Greek tax on Greek rental income at 15% up to €12,000, 25% to €24,000, 35% to €36,000 and 45% above, after a flat 5% deduction for expenses.

## Buying a home in Italy: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes for EU citizens; non-EU buyers need reciprocity (US, UK, Canada, Australia qualify).

Costs on top of the price
4-15% · Registration tax 9% on a second home (resale), or VAT on new builds; notary 1-2% + legal ~1% + agent ~3% (GPG roundtrip 10-18%).

Yearly property tax
IMU 0.4-1.06% on second homes (on cadastral value).

Tax on rental income
Optional flat 'cedolare secca' on short lets: 21% for one property, 26% from the second.

What holiday rentals earn
No sourced STR gross yield found. Cheap Italian homes are usually old stock in depopulating towns, not new builds.

Long-term rent yield
5.0-8.8 (GPG Q3 2026: national 6.61, Catania 8.75, Palermo 7.84, Milan 4.97)% gross

Holiday-rental rules
Every tourist let needs a national CIN code shown on listings and at the property; from the 3rd property it is treated as a business (VAT registration).

## Buying a home in Japan: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes. Foreigners can buy freehold land and homes on the same terms as Japanese citizens, even on a tourist visa, though buying does not give a visa or residency.

Costs on top of the price
6-9% · The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.

Yearly property tax
Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

Tax on rental income
Rent paid to a non-resident is subject to 20.42% withholding (except when an individual rents it as their own home), and the owner must file a tax return each year through a tax representative in Japan to settle the final tax.

## Buying a home in Lombok: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Same Indonesian rules as Bali: no freehold; leasehold, Hak Pakai, or HGB via a PT PMA.

Costs on top of the price
6.5-18% · BPHTB 5% + notary 1-2.5% + legal 0.5-1.5%; +11% PPN/VAT on new developer units unless the 2026 VAT incentive applies.

Yearly property tax
PBB, up to ~0.5% of assessed (NJOP-based) value.

Tax on rental income
Non-residents: 20% withholding on gross rent (10% possible under a treaty); PT PMA 22% corporate tax.

What holiday rentals earn
No independent gross-yield figure found. Airbtics (Feb 2025-Jan 2026) South Lombok: 64% occupancy, ADR ~US$78, median revenue ~US$18k/yr, graded C+ and in the lowest 48% for STR yield in Southeast Asia. Developer projections (Lombok International Development) of 6.8-14.8% NET are not independent.

Holiday-rental rules
Pondok Wisata licence required for short-term rental; foreigners must operate through a PT PMA.

## Buying a home in Mexico: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes, but in the Restricted Zone (within 50 km of the coast or 100 km of borders, which covers Tulum and Playa del Carmen) only through a fideicomiso bank trust or a Mexican company; direct ownership elsewhere.

Costs on top of the price
3.5-8% · Acquisition tax 2-5% + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-1.5% (GPG 3.5-7.5%), plus 0.5-1.5% for fideicomiso/permit setup; TheLatinvestor budgets 5-8%.

Yearly property tax
Municipal predial, set locally on cadastral value; usually small, often less than HOA fees.

Tax on rental income
Non-residents: 25% ISR withholding on gross rent; plus 16% IVA on short-term stays (Airbnb remits on its bookings).

What holiday rentals earn
No sourced STR gross yield. AirDNA (early 2026, via Virestia): Tulum average occupancy 44%, 8,000+ listings, bottom 80% of condos earn US$13-18k/yr at 31-44% occupancy. TheLatinvestor: Tulum ADR US$125, down 23% YoY.

Long-term rent yield
4.6-6.1 (GPG Q2 2026: Merida 6.08, Cancun 4.60, national 5.79)% gross

Holiday-rental rules
Quintana Roo: mandatory RETUR-Q registration (since Aug 2025, renewed annually) plus a state operating licence and RFC tax ID; 6% lodging tax; fines up to MXN 100,000.

## Buying a home in Montenegro: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes, houses and apartments freely; land requires a local company.

Costs on top of the price
1-4% · New build: 21% VAT is normally included in the developer price, buyer pays notary + ~1% legal; resale: 3% transfer tax (progressive on higher values) + notary + ~1% legal (GPG 4.01%).

Yearly property tax
Municipal, ~0.25-1% of assessed value (higher rates possible for tourist properties).

Tax on rental income
Around 15% withholding for non-residents.

What holiday rentals earn
No sourced STR gross yield found.

Long-term rent yield
4.4-5.2 (GPG Q2 2026: Podgorica 5.15, Budva 5.01, Tivat 4.36, national 4.84)% gross

Holiday-rental rules
Short-term rentals must be registered and pay a municipal tourist tax per guest-night.

## Buying a home in the Netherlands: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes. There are no nationality or residence rules and no surcharge for foreign buyers. Some cities, such as The Hague, restrict renting out cheaper homes after purchase without a permit (opkoopbescherming).

Costs on top of the price
2-9% · Transfer tax (overdrachtsbelasting) of 8% if you will not live in the home, such as a buy-to-let or holiday home, or 2% if it becomes your main home; a notary fee for the transfer deed of around EUR 500; Kadaster registration fees; and mortgage costs if you borrow; the seller pays its own agent.

Yearly property tax
Owners pay municipal property tax (onroerendezaakbelasting, OZB) on the official WOZ value, at a rate each municipality sets, which in practice is a per mille figure; tenants of homes do not pay it.

Tax on rental income
Non-residents declare Dutch property in box 3, where tax is 36% on a deemed return of 6% of the property's value in 2026, after a tax-free allowance of EUR 59,357 per person, regardless of actual rent.

## Buying a home in Northern Cyprus: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes, up to 3 properties (land cap ~1,338 m2), but each needs Council of Ministers Permission to Purchase (1-6 months); title-deed history risk.

Costs on top of the price
12-22% · Title deed transfer fee for foreigners 6-12% (sources disagree: 9% most cited, 12% in one 2026 guide) + 5% VAT on new builds (one source says 19%) + 0.5% stamp duty + legal GBP 1,000-2,500 + transformer fee GBP 1,500-3,000 on new builds.

Yearly property tax
Per m2, very low: about GBP 10-100/yr for a typical apartment or villa.

Tax on rental income
10% of gross rental income (Investra, 2026).

What holiday rentals earn
No sourced gross yield; data conflict. Airbtics Jan 2026 Iskele: 75% occupancy, ADR EUR 84, ~EUR 24k/yr, 'top 1%' for STR yield in Southern Europe. AirROI 2025-26 Kyrenia: 37.1% occupancy, ADR US$99, ~US$10k/yr.

Holiday-rental rules
Must register with the Ministry of Tourism and hold a licence for short-term letting; monthly tax reporting.

## Buying a home in Norway: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes. Anyone with the funds can buy property in Norway, and a built plot of up to 2 decares normally needs no concession (konsesjon) or self-declaration; owning property gives no right to live there.

Costs on top of the price
2.5-3% · Document duty (dokumentavgift) of 2.5% of market value, a registration fee (tinglysingsgebyr) of NOK 545 for the deed and NOK 545 for any mortgage document; a flat in a housing cooperative (borettslag) has no document duty; the seller normally pays the agent.

Yearly property tax
Some municipalities charge property tax (eiendomsskatt), at most 4 per mille of the value after a reduction of at least 30%, and some also give a basic deduction; many charge nothing.

Tax on rental income
Rental profit is normally taxed at 22%, and the Tax Administration says its rental rules also apply to owners who are tax resident abroad.

- [globalpropertyguide.com/europe/norway/buying-guide](https://www.globalpropertyguide.com/europe/norway/buying-guide)

## Buying a home in Poland: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
EU, EEA and Swiss citizens buy on the same terms as Poles. Other foreigners can buy an apartment without a permit, but usually need a permit from the Ministry of the Interior (MSWiA) to buy a house or land.

Costs on top of the price
2.5-4% · Tax on civil law transactions (PCC) 2% of the value, paid by the buyer within 14 days of the deed; notary fee (taksa notarialna) capped at PLN 1,010 plus 0.4% of the value above PLN 60,000, plus 23% VAT; court fee of PLN 200 to enter ownership in the land register (plus PLN 100 for a new register); optional lawyer about 1%; the agent fee (about 2-3%) depends on the agreement.

Yearly property tax
Owners pay a local property tax (podatek od nieruchomości) set by the commune, capped in 2026 at PLN 1.25 per m² of usable floor space for flats and houses.

Tax on rental income
Private rental income is taxed as a flat lump sum (ryczałt) of 8.5% of revenue up to PLN 100,000 a year and 12.5% above that.

## Buying a home in Portugal: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes, same rights as Portuguese citizens (IMT increase for foreign second-home buyers announced Sept 2025).

Costs on top of the price
3-12% · IMT transfer tax 0-8% (progressive) + stamp duty 0.8% + notary/registry 0.9-1.2% + legal 1.25-2%.

Yearly property tax
IMI 0.3-0.45% of taxable value (urban), set by municipality.

Tax on rental income
Long-term: 25% flat for non-residents; short-term (AL) under the simplified regime only 35-50% of gross is taxable.

What holiday rentals earn
No sourced STR gross yield found.

Long-term rent yield
3.8-4.9 (GPG Q2 2026: national 4.29, Lisbon 3.76, Porto 3.96, Faro 4.48)% gross

Holiday-rental rules
Alojamento Local (AL) registration is mandatory; since Nov 2024 municipalities can freeze new AL licences in containment zones (Lisbon, Porto use this); condominiums can object with >50% of owners.

## Buying a home in Spain: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes, no restrictions at present; the government has proposed a 100% tax on (or ban for) non-EU non-resident buyers, not enacted.

Costs on top of the price
7.5-14% · New build: 10% IVA + 0.5-1.5% AJD stamp duty + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-2%; resale: ITP transfer tax 6-11% instead of IVA/AJD.

Yearly property tax
IBI 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value (municipal), plus imputed income tax on unlet homes.

Tax on rental income
Non-residents: EU/EEA 19% on net income; non-EU 24% on gross with no deductions.

Holiday-rental yield
5-7% gross

What holiday rentals earn
Gross, Global Investments guide 2026 for Costa del Sol, Valencia, Canary Islands; realistic net 3-4.5% before tax. GPG long-term: national 5.51%, Alicante 6.80, Murcia 6.06, Malaga 4.97.

Long-term rent yield
4.7-6.8 (GPG Q3 2026, national 5.51)% gross

Holiday-rental rules
Regional tourist licence plus the national single rental registry number (mandatory since 1 Jul 2025); new tourist lets in apartment blocks need 3/5 owners' approval (since 3 Apr 2025).

## Buying a home in Sweden: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes. There are no citizenship or residence rules for buying a home in Sweden, but you need a Swedish personal identity number or coordination number (samordningsnummer) to register ownership.

Costs on top of the price
1.5-3.5% · Stamp duty on the title (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price or tax value, whichever is higher, plus a SEK 825 fee; if you borrow and need new mortgage deeds (pantbrev), 2% of their amount plus a SEK 375 fee; optional legal advice; the seller normally pays the agent, and a cooperative flat (bostadsrätt) has no lagfart.

Yearly property tax
Houses pay a municipal property fee (kommunal fastighetsavgift) of SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.

Tax on rental income
Non-resident individuals pay 30% tax on net rental income as capital income; for a private home you can first deduct SEK 40,000 per property and 20% of the rent (the 20% does not apply to a bostadsrätt).

## Buying a home in Switzerland: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Under the Lex Koller law, EU/EFTA citizens living in Switzerland and holders of a C permit buy like Swiss citizens, and non-EU holders of a B permit can buy a home they live in. People living abroad need a cantonal permit and can usually only buy one holiday home in a tourist area, within national quotas; a proposed tightening was under consultation in 2026.

Costs on top of the price
1-5% · Transfer tax (Handänderungssteuer, droits de mutation) 0% to about 3.3% depending on the canton; notary about 0.1-0.5%; land register fee, a small fixed amount or percentage; optional lawyer 1-2%; the agent fee (2-3%) is paid by the seller.

Yearly property tax
More than half of the cantons charge an annual property tax (Liegenschaftssteuer), usually 0.01-0.3% of the assessed value, and owners also pay cantonal wealth tax on the property value minus the mortgage.

Tax on rental income
Non-residents pay tax on net Swiss rental income at ordinary cantonal and communal rates plus federal direct tax, and some cantons set the rate using worldwide income.

## Buying a home in the United Kingdom: what it really costs

Can foreigners buy?
Yes. There are no nationality restrictions on buying homes anywhere in the UK and no visa is needed, but buying does not give a right to live there.

Costs on top of the price
3-9% · In England and Northern Ireland, Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) is 0% up to £125,000 and 2% from £125,001 to £250,000, plus a 2% surcharge for non-UK residents and a further 5% if you already own a home anywhere, so a non-resident who owns another home pays 7% up to £125,000 and 9% to £250,000; solicitor (conveyancer) about 0.6-1% with a typical minimum of around £2,100 including VAT; Land Registry fee £20 to £230; searches extra; the seller pays the estate agent.

Yearly property tax
Owners or occupiers pay council tax to the local council, and many councils in England charge second homes a premium of up to 100% from April 2025.

Tax on rental income
Non-resident landlords pay UK income tax on rent at 20%, 40% or 45%, with 20% deducted at source by the agent or tenant unless HMRC approves gross payment, and the rates on property income are set to rise to 22%, 42% and 47% from April 2027.
