## How to buy a home in France as a foreigner

The steps, papers and taxes, in plain words. General information, not legal advice: use a local lawyer before you sign.

### Can foreigners buy?

Yes. Foreigners can buy property in France without major restrictions, and non-EU buyers do not need a permit, although the paperwork can take longer.

### The steps

- Make an offer: Agree the price with the seller, usually through the agent. Budget for notary fees and other costs first.
- Sign the preliminary contract: Sign the compromis de vente with a notary (notaire). Add conditions (clauses suspensives) such as getting a mortgage.
- Use the cooling-off period: You have 10 days after receiving the signed compromis to withdraw without penalty. The seller cannot withdraw.
- Pay the deposit: After the cooling-off period, pay a deposit, usually 10% of the price. You may lose it if you pull out without a valid condition.
- Let the notary run checks: The notary checks ownership, boundaries and rights of way and collects the compulsory diagnostic surveys (termites, lead, asbestos).
- Sign the final deed: Send the balance and fees to the notary's account before the date, then sign the acte de vente in person or by power of attorney. The notary registers the sale.

### Costs on top of the price

About 7-8.5%: Transfer taxes (droits de mutation) of about 5.8%, or about 6.3% in departments that raised their rate for 2025 to March 2028; notary fee (émoluments) on a sliding scale from 3.87% down to 0.799% plus 20% VAT, about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; land security contribution (contribution de sécurité immobilière) 0.10%; disbursements (débours) of about €800 to €1,200; the agent fee is usually built into the advertised price (FAI) and paid by the seller, sometimes shared.

### Every year

Expect the annual taxe foncière, plus taxe d'habitation if the home is a furnished second home, and income tax and social charges on any rent.

Yearly property tax: Owners pay an annual property tax (taxe foncière) set by the local authorities, and owners of a furnished second home also pay housing tax (taxe d'habitation), which some communes raise by a surcharge of 5% to 60%.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay French income tax on French rental income at a minimum rate of 20% (30% above about €27,500), plus social charges of 17.2%, or 7.5% for people covered by social security in another EU/EEA country or Switzerland.

## How to buy a home in Germany as a foreigner

The steps, papers and taxes, in plain words. General information, not legal advice: use a local lawyer before you sign.

### Can foreigners buy?

Yes. There are no restrictions on foreigners buying property in Germany, though non-EU buyers usually need a bigger down payment to get a loan.

### The steps

- Find a home and arrange money: Search the portals or use a local agent and get financing in place before signing.
- Get independent advice: The notary is neutral and does not act for you, so consider your own lawyer and a survey.
- Sign before a notary: The notary drafts the purchase contract and both sides sign it in front of the notary; you can sign through a certified power of attorney from abroad.
- Secure a priority notice: The notary registers a priority notice (Vormerkung) in the land register to protect you against other sales.
- Pay the transfer tax and the price: Pay the transfer tax when the tax office sends the bill, and pay the price as the contract sets out, often via the notary.
- Get registered as owner: The land registry (Grundbuch) enters you as owner once the transfer tax is paid, which can take 3 to 4 months.

### Costs on top of the price

About 5-8.5%: Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) of 3.5% to 6.5% depending on the state (3.5% in Bavaria, 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein), plus notary and land registry fees (Notar- und Grundbuchkosten) of about 1.5-2%; if the seller hired the agent, the buyer pays half the commission by law, which is extra.

### Every year

Expect the municipal property tax, insurance, utilities and upkeep. Rental profit is taxable in Germany, so a non-resident landlord deals with a German tax office.

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property tax (Grundsteuer), calculated since 2025 as assessed value x a tax rate x a municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) that each municipality sets.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident owners are taxed in Germany on net rental income at the normal progressive income tax rates, but without the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag).

## Property glossary by country: the local words of buying a home abroad

Every country names the same steps differently: the paper that shows who owns the house, the contract before the contract, the tax on the purchase. These glossaries keep each word as it is written where you will hear it and explain it in plain English.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

### All 90 words, A to Z

[acte de vente](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/france#acte-de-vente) · France
The final deed, signed before the notary (notaire).

[AFM](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/greece#afm) · Greece
The Greek tax number.

[Agentsiya po vpisvaniyata](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/bulgaria#agentsiya-po-vpisvaniyata) · Bulgaria
The Registry Agency, where the notary files the deed.

[akiya](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/japan#akiya) · Japan
A vacant house.

[APE](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/italy#ape) · Italy
The energy performance certificate of the home.

[arras](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/spain#arras) · Spain
A private contract with a deposit that reserves the home before the deed is signed.

[Auflassungsvormerkung](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/germany#auflassungsvormerkung) · Germany
A notice entered in the land register that protects the buyer's claim until the transfer is registered.

[bank- og advokatforbehold](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#advokatforbehold) · Sweden and Denmark
Clauses that make a Danish purchase contract depend on the approval of your bank and your lawyer.

[bedenktijd](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/netherlands#bedenktijd) · Netherlands
Three days in which the buyer can cancel without a reason and without paying the seller anything.

[BSN](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/netherlands#bsn) · Netherlands
The citizen service number used for tax and official business.

[budgivning](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#budgivning) · Sweden and Denmark
The round of bids for a home in Sweden.

[buyer's agent agreement](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#buyer-agent-agreement) · Mexico and the United States
The written agreement a buyer signs with an agent before being shown homes in the United States.

[caderneta predial](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/portugal#caderneta-predial) · Portugal
The tax office's record of the property, with its tax value and whether it is urban or rustic.

[certidão permanente](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/portugal#certidao-permanente) · Portugal
The land registry certificate of a property, kept online and always up to date.

[chūkai tesūryō](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/japan#chukai-tesuryo) · Japan
The estate agent's fee, paid by the buyer and capped by rule.

[closing](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#closing) · Mexico and the United States
The meeting at which the balance and the closing costs are paid and the sale completes.

[codice fiscale](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/italy#codice-fiscale) · Italy
The personal tax code you need for any contract in Italy.

[compromesso](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/italy#compromesso) · Italy
The preliminary contract that binds both sides to sign the deed later.

[compromis de vente](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/france#compromis-de-vente) · France
The preliminary contract in which seller and buyer both commit to the sale.

[conditions suspensives](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/france#conditions-suspensives) · France
Conditions written into the contract that must be met for the sale to go ahead, such as getting the mortgage.

[conformità urbanistica e catastale](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/italy#conformita) · Italy
Proof that the building as it stands matches its permits and its cadastral plans.

[CPCV](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/portugal#cpcv) · Portugal
The promissory contract that fixes the price and the date of the deed.

[danachna otsenka](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/bulgaria#danachna-otsenka) · Bulgaria
The tax assessment value of the property, on which the yearly municipal tax is charged.

[danak pri pridobivane na imushtestva](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/bulgaria#mesten-danak) · Bulgaria
The municipal tax on acquiring property.

[délai de rétractation](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/france#delai-de-retractation) · France
Ten calendar days in which a private buyer of a home can withdraw without giving a reason.

[DPE](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/france#dpe) · France
The energy performance survey of the home, one of the surveys the seller must provide.

[E9](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/greece#e9) · Greece
The declaration in which an owner lists the properties held in Greece.

[ejendomsværdiskat](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#ejendomsvaerdiskat) · Sweden and Denmark
The two yearly property taxes in Denmark: one on the value of the home and one on the land.

[ejido](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#ejido) · Mexico and the United States
Communal agricultural land, which cannot be sold in the normal way.

[ENFIA](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/greece#enfia) · Greece
The unified yearly property tax.

[escritura](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/spain#escritura) · Spain
The deed of sale, signed in front of a notary.

[escritura](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/portugal#escritura-pt) · Portugal
The deed of sale, signed at a notary or at a Casa Pronta desk.

[escritura pública](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#escritura-mx) · Mexico and the United States
The public deed, prepared and signed by a public notary.

[escrow](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#escrow) · Mexico and the United States
An account set up by the mortgage lender to pay property taxes and home insurance out of your monthly payment.

[fideicomiso](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#fideicomiso) · Mexico and the United States
A bank trust in which a Mexican bank holds the title for a foreign buyer in the restricted zone.

[FIRPTA](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#firpta) · Mexico and the United States
The rule under which the buyer generally withholds 15% of the sale price when a foreign owner sells.

[fóros metavívasis](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/greece#foros-metavivasis) · Greece
The property transfer tax, paid before the final deed.

[frais de notaire](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/france#frais-de-notaire) · France
Everything paid through the notary at the sale: mostly transfer taxes, plus the notary's own fee.

[Grundbuch](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/germany#grundbuch) · Germany
The land register, where owners and charges are entered.

[Grunderwerbsteuer](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/germany#grunderwerbsteuer) · Germany
The transfer tax on buying property, set by each federal state.

[Grundsteuer](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/germany#grundsteuer) · Germany
The yearly municipal property tax.

[HOA dues](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#hoa-dues) · Mexico and the United States
The fees paid to the owners' association of a condo building or a planned community.

[home inspection](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#home-inspection) · Mexico and the United States
An inspection of the condition of the house, often part of the buying process.

[IBI](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/spain#ibi) · Spain
The yearly property tax charged by the town hall.

[IMI](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/portugal#imi) · Portugal
The yearly municipal property tax.

[imposta di registro](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/italy#imposta-di-registro) · Italy
The tax on buying from a private seller.

[IMT](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/portugal#imt) · Portugal
The transfer tax on the purchase, on a sliding scale.

[IMU](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/italy#imu) · Italy
The yearly municipal tax on second homes.

[ISAI](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#isai) · Mexico and the United States
The tax on acquiring property in Mexico.

[ITP](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/spain#itp) · Spain
The tax the buyer pays on a resale home, set by each region.

[jūyō jikō setsumei](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/japan#juyo-jiko-setsumei) · Japan
The explanation of the property's legal status that a licensed specialist must give the buyer before the contract.

[Kadaster](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/netherlands#kadaster) · Netherlands
The national land registry.

[kommunal fastighetsavgift](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#fastighetsavgift) · Sweden and Denmark
The yearly municipal property fee on houses in Sweden.

[koopovereenkomst](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/netherlands#koopovereenkomst) · Netherlands
The written purchase agreement; only this, once signed, binds a private buyer.

[köpekontrakt](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#kopekontrakt) · Sweden and Denmark
The purchase contract signed by buyer and seller in Sweden.

[kosten koper](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/netherlands#kosten-koper) · Netherlands
A price marked k.k. means the buyer pays the transfer tax and the notary's transfer deed on top.

[kotei shisan zei](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/japan#kotei-shisan-zei) · Japan
The yearly tax on land and buildings.

[Ktimatológio](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/greece#ktimatologio) · Greece
The Hellenic Cadastre, where deeds are registered.

[lagfart](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#lagfart) · Sweden and Denmark
The registration of the buyer as owner at Lantmäteriet, the Swedish land registry.

[NIE](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/spain#nie) · Spain
The identity and tax number Spain gives to foreigners.

[NIF](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/portugal#nif) · Portugal
The Portuguese tax number, needed before anything is signed.

[nota simple](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/spain#nota-simple) · Spain
A short extract from the Land Registry that identifies the property, who holds rights over it and what charges it carries.

[Notar](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/germany#notar) · Germany
The public official who must record the purchase contract for it to be valid.

[Notar- und Grundbuchkosten](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/germany#notar-und-grundbuchkosten) · Germany
The notary's and the land register's fees for the purchase.

[notarialen akt](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/bulgaria#notarialen-akt) · Bulgaria
The notarial deed that transfers the property.

[nōzei kanrinin](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/japan#nozei-kanrinin) · Japan
A person with a Japanese address who receives and pays the tax bills of an owner who lives abroad.

[overdrachtsbelasting](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/netherlands#overdrachtsbelasting) · Netherlands
The transfer tax on buying property.

[OZB](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/netherlands#ozb) · Netherlands
The yearly municipal property tax, charged on the official value of the home (the WOZ value).

[pantbrev](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#pantbrev) · Sweden and Denmark
A mortgage deed on the property, needed if you borrow against it.

[paramethóries periochés](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/greece#border-areas) · Greece
Designated border areas, where buyers from outside the EU and EFTA need a permit.

[plusvalía municipal](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/spain#plusvalia) · Spain
A municipal tax on the increase in value of urban land, which comes due when the property changes hands.

[predial](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#predial) · Mexico and the United States
The yearly local property tax in Mexico.

[predvaritelen dogovor](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/bulgaria#predvaritelen-dogovor) · Bulgaria
The preliminary contract signed before the notarial deed.

[promesse de vente](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/france#promesse-de-vente) · France
A contract in which only the seller commits, giving the buyer an option to buy for a set time.

[proposta d'acquisto](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/italy#proposta) · Italy
The written offer to buy, usually with a small deposit.

[prosýmfono](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/greece#prosymfono) · Greece
The private preliminary agreement signed before the notary's deed.

[rogito](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/italy#rogito) · Italy
The final deed of sale, signed before a notary (notaio).

[samordningsnummer](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#samordningsnummer) · Sweden and Denmark
The identity number Sweden gives to people who are not registered as living there.

[shihō shoshi](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/japan#shiho-shoshi) · Japan
The judicial scrivener, the professional who registers the transfer of ownership.

[skøde](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#skode) · Sweden and Denmark
The Danish deed; its digital registration (tinglysning) with the Land Registration Court makes you the legal owner.

[sommerhus](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#sommerhus) · Sweden and Denmark
A Danish holiday home.

[suelo rústico](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/spain#suelo-rustico) · Spain
Land classed as rural, where building is restricted.

[taxe foncière](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/france#taxe-fonciere) · France
The yearly property tax paid by the owner, set by the local authorities.

[tetsukekin](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/japan#tetsukekin) · Japan
The deposit paid when the sale contract is signed.

[tilladelse fra Civilstyrelsen](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/sweden-denmark#civilstyrelsen) · Sweden and Denmark
The permission that a buyer without Danish domicile, or without five years of past residence, needs to buy a home in Denmark.

[title insurance](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#title-insurance) · Mexico and the United States
Insurance against problems with the title, such as someone with a legal claim on the home.

[visura catastale](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/italy#visura-catastale) · Italy
The extract of the cadastre for a property: its identification, class and cadastral income.

[VvE](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/netherlands#vve) · Netherlands
The owners' association of an apartment building.

[zemya](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/bulgaria#zemya) · Bulgaria
Land, which a buyer from outside the EU cannot own in their own name.

[zona restringida](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary/mexico-united-states#zona-restringida) · Mexico and the United States

Glossary · Bulgarian

## Buying a home in Bulgaria: the local words, explained

Bulgaria has some of the lowest yearly costs in our files and one rule that changes everything for buyers from outside the EU: buildings yes, land no. The words below are in Cyrillic with their reading.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- predvaritelen dogovor
- notarialen akt
- Agentsiya po vpisvaniyata
- zemya
- danachna otsenka
- danak pri pridobivane na imushtestva

#### predvaritelen dogovor preliminary contract

Also: предварителен договор

The preliminary contract signed before the notarial deed.

You pay a deposit, usually 10%. If you pull out you lose it, and if the seller pulls out they owe you double.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Bulgaria](https://realhunt.co/costs/bulgaria)

#### notarialen akt notarial deed

Also: нотариален акт

The notarial deed that transfers the property.

It is signed before a notary in the district of the property, with a sworn translator if you do not speak Bulgarian. Payments of EUR 5,113 or more must go by bank transfer.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Bulgaria](https://realhunt.co/costs/bulgaria)

#### Agentsiya po vpisvaniyata Registry Agency

Also: Агенция по вписванията

The Registry Agency, where the notary files the deed.

Filing usually takes one to three business days. Before that, a lawyer checks the title and the debts, which usually takes five to ten business days.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Bulgaria](https://realhunt.co/costs/bulgaria)

#### zemya land

Also: земя

Land, which a buyer from outside the EU cannot own in their own name.

Non-EU citizens can buy apartments and buildings in their own name. To buy a house with its plot, they usually set up a Bulgarian company, which adds about EUR 500 to 1,500 a year in running costs.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Bulgaria](https://realhunt.co/costs/bulgaria)

#### danachna otsenka tax assessment value and the yearly tax on it

Also: данъчна оценка

The tax assessment value of the property, on which the yearly municipal tax is charged.

The municipal property tax is 0.01% to 0.45% of that value, with a 5% discount if paid in full by 30 April, plus a municipal waste collection fee. You must file a tax declaration with the municipality within two months of buying.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Bulgaria](https://realhunt.co/costs/bulgaria)

#### danak pri pridobivane na imushtestva municipal transfer tax

Also: данък при придобиване на имущества

The municipal tax on acquiring property.

Each municipality sets it between 0.1% and 3%; Sofia charges 2.5%. Notary fees of 0.1% to 1.5%, legal fees of 0.5% to 1% and an agent's 2.5% to 3% come on top.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Bulgaria](https://realhunt.co/costs/bulgaria)

Glossary · French

## Buying a home in France: the local words, explained

French sales run through the notary and through two words that look alike, promesse and compromis. This page explains them, the ten days you have to change your mind and the surveys the seller must hand over.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- compromis de vente
- promesse de vente
- délai de rétractation
- conditions suspensives
- DPE
- frais de notaire
- acte de vente
- taxe foncière

#### compromis de vente preliminary contract binding both sides

Also: promesse synallagmatique de vente

The preliminary contract in which seller and buyer both commit to the sale.

The notaries of France put it plainly: legally, the compromis is already a sale. It usually comes with a deposit (dépôt de garantie) of 5% to 10% of the price, held in the notary's blocked account and deducted from the price at the final deed.

Sources: [Notaires de France](https://www.notaires.fr/index.php/fr/immobilier-fiscalite/achat-et-vente-les-etapes/la-promesse-de-vente-et-le-compromis-de-vente) · [Service-Public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F2965)

#### promesse de vente one-sided promise to sell

Also: promesse unilatérale de vente

A contract in which only the seller commits, giving the buyer an option to buy for a set time.

The option generally lasts two to three months and the seller cannot back out meanwhile. The buyer pays an indemnité d'immobilisation, in principle 10% of the price, which the seller keeps if the buyer does not go ahead, except during the withdrawal period or when a condition such as the loan fails.

Sources: [Notaires de France](https://www.notaires.fr/index.php/fr/immobilier-fiscalite/achat-et-vente-les-etapes/la-promesse-de-vente-et-le-compromis-de-vente) · [Service-Public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F2965)

#### délai de rétractation withdrawal period

Ten calendar days in which a private buyer of a home can withdraw without giving a reason.

The period starts the day after the registered letter with the signed contract is first presented to the buyer. If you withdraw in time, what you paid is returned in full. The seller has no such right.

Sources: [Service-Public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F2965) · [Notaires de France](https://www.notaires.fr/index.php/fr/immobilier-fiscalite/achat-et-vente-les-etapes/la-promesse-de-vente-et-le-compromis-de-vente)

#### conditions suspensives conditions that must be met

Also: clauses suspensives

Conditions written into the contract that must be met for the sale to go ahead, such as getting the mortgage.

If a condition is not met, the deposit is returned in full. If the buyer simply gives up after the withdrawal period, the seller keeps it.

Source: [Service-Public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F2965)

#### DPE energy rating

Also: diagnostic de performance énergétique

The energy performance survey of the home, one of the surveys the seller must provide.

It belongs to the technical survey file (dossier de diagnostic technique) attached to the preliminary contract or the deed. Depending on the house, the file also holds a lead report (built before 1 January 1949), an asbestos report (building permit before 1 July 1997), reports on electricity and gas installations older than 15 years, termites in declared areas and the septic system when the house is not on mains drainage. A house rated E, F or G also needs an energy audit.

Source: [Service-Public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F10798)

#### frais de notaire the notary's bill, mostly tax

Everything paid through the notary at the sale: mostly transfer taxes, plus the notary's own fee.

Our France file breaks it down: transfer taxes (droits de mutation) of about 5.8%, or about 6.3% in departments that raised their rate until March 2028; the notary's fee (émoluments) on a sliding scale, about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; a 0.10% land security contribution; and €800 to €1,200 of disbursements.

Source: [RealHunt country file: France](https://realhunt.co/costs/france)

#### acte de vente the final deed

Also: acte authentique

The final deed, signed before the notary (notaire).

You send the balance and the fees to the notary's account before the date and sign in person or by power of attorney; the notary then registers the sale.

Source: [RealHunt country file: France](https://realhunt.co/costs/france)

#### taxe foncière yearly property tax

The yearly property tax paid by the owner, set by the local authorities.

Owners of a furnished second home also pay the housing tax (taxe d'habitation), which some communes raise by a surcharge of 5% to 60%.

Source: [RealHunt country file: France](https://realhunt.co/costs/france)

Glossary · German

## Buying a home in Germany: the local words, explained

In Germany nothing about a house is binding until a notary has recorded it, and you are not the owner until the land register says so. These are the words for each stage.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- Notar
- Grundbuch
- Auflassungsvormerkung
- Grunderwerbsteuer
- Notar- und Grundbuchkosten
- Grundsteuer

#### Notar notary

Also: notarielle Beurkundung

The public official who must record the purchase contract for it to be valid.

Section 311b of the Civil Code requires notarial recording for any contract that obliges someone to transfer or acquire land. The notary drafts the contract and both sides sign in front of the notary, but the notary is neutral and does not act for the buyer, so our Germany guide suggests your own lawyer and a survey.

Sources: [Bundesministerium der Justiz](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__311b.html) · [RealHunt country file: Germany](https://realhunt.co/costs/germany)

#### Grundbuch land register

The land register, where owners and charges are entered.

It is not open to everyone: section 12 of the Land Register Code allows inspection to anyone who shows a legitimate interest. You become the owner when the register enters you, once the transfer tax is paid, which our Germany guide says can take three to four months.

Sources: [Bundesministerium der Justiz](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gbo/__12.html) · [RealHunt country file: Germany](https://realhunt.co/costs/germany)

#### Auflassungsvormerkung priority notice

Also: Vormerkung

A notice entered in the land register that protects the buyer's claim until the transfer is registered.

Under section 883 of the Civil Code, once the notice is entered, any later disposal of the property is ineffective as far as it would defeat the buyer's claim, even one made through enforcement or by an insolvency administrator. In our Germany guide the notary registers it after the contract is signed, to protect the buyer against other sales.

Sources: [Bundesministerium der Justiz](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__883.html) · [RealHunt country file: Germany](https://realhunt.co/costs/germany)

#### Grunderwerbsteuer property transfer tax

The transfer tax on buying property, set by each federal state.

Our Germany file gives 3.5% to 6.5% of the price: 3.5% in Bavaria and 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein. The tax office sends the bill after the contract, and the land register does not enter you until it is paid.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Germany](https://realhunt.co/costs/germany)

#### Notar- und Grundbuchkosten notary and land register fees

The notary's and the land register's fees for the purchase.

About 1.5% to 2% of the price, on top of the transfer tax. If the seller hired the estate agent, the buyer pays half the commission by law, which is extra.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Germany](https://realhunt.co/costs/germany)

#### Grundsteuer yearly property tax

Also: Hebesatz

The yearly municipal property tax.

Since 2025 it is calculated as the assessed value times a tax rate times a multiplier (Hebesatz) that each municipality sets, so two similar houses in neighbouring towns can pay different amounts.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Germany](https://realhunt.co/costs/germany)

Glossary · Greek

## Buying a home in Greece: the local words, explained

A Greek purchase starts with a tax number and ends with two tax forms that follow you every year you own the house. These are the words, in Greek letters and in ours.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- AFM
- prosýmfono
- fóros metavívasis
- Ktimatológio
- E9
- ENFIA
- paramethóries periochés

#### AFM Greek tax number

Also: ΑΦΜ

The Greek tax number.

You apply with your passport. It is free and needed to sign contracts and pay taxes.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Greece](https://realhunt.co/costs/greece)

#### prosýmfono preliminary agreement

Also: προσύμφωνο

The private preliminary agreement signed before the notary's deed.

It comes with a deposit, usually 5% to 10%, which you normally lose if you withdraw.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Greece](https://realhunt.co/costs/greece)

#### fóros metavívasis transfer tax

Also: φόρος μεταβίβασης ακινήτων

The property transfer tax, paid before the final deed.

It is 3.09% of the price or of the taxable value, whichever is higher. The notary prepares the declaration. The government has announced a 15% transfer tax for buyers from outside the EU from 1 January 2027, which was not final when our Greece file was last checked in September 2026.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Greece](https://realhunt.co/costs/greece)

#### Ktimatológio the cadastre

Also: Κτηματολόγιο

The Hellenic Cadastre, where deeds are registered.

After signing before the notary, the deed is registered at the local land registry or cadastre. Before that, a lawyer searches it for mortgages, liens and claims.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Greece](https://realhunt.co/costs/greece)

#### E9 property declaration

Also: Ε9

The declaration in which an owner lists the properties held in Greece.

The tax authority (AADE) tells owners who live abroad to file it when they acquire a property or when anything changes in the property they hold in Greece. The yearly tax is worked out from it.

Source: [AADE (Independent Authority for Public Revenue)](https://www.aade.gr/en/greeks-abroad-non-residents/property-taxation/unified-tax-ownership-real-estate-e9-enfia)

#### ENFIA yearly property tax

Also: ΕΝΦΙΑ

The unified yearly property tax.

AADE calculates it each year for the properties that exist on 1 January, and it can be paid in up to ten equal monthly instalments. Our Greece file adds that it depends on the location, size, age and official zone value of each property, with an extra charge when the total exceeds €500,000.

Sources: [AADE (Independent Authority for Public Revenue)](https://www.aade.gr/en/greeks-abroad-non-residents/property-taxation/unified-tax-ownership-real-estate-e9-enfia) · [RealHunt country file: Greece](https://realhunt.co/costs/greece)

#### paramethóries periochés border areas, where some buyers need a permit

Also: παραμεθόριες περιοχές

Designated border areas, where buyers from outside the EU and EFTA need a permit.

The areas include parts of northern Greece and eastern Aegean islands such as the Dodecanese and Rhodes. The application is made while the lawyer checks the title.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Greece](https://realhunt.co/costs/greece)

Glossary · Italian

## Buying a home in Italy: the local words, explained

The Italian words on the path from an offer to the keys: the tax code, the two contracts, the notary's deed and the papers that prove the house matches its plans.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- codice fiscale
- proposta d'acquisto
- compromesso
- rogito
- visura catastale
- conformità urbanistica e catastale
- APE
- imposta di registro
- IMU

#### codice fiscale Italian tax code

The personal tax code you need for any contract in Italy.

It is free. You ask for it at the tax agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) in Italy or at an Italian consulate abroad, and it is the first step of our Italy guide.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Italy](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy)

#### proposta d'acquisto written offer

The written offer to buy, usually with a small deposit.

Once the seller accepts it, many buyers go on to sign the preliminary contract.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Italy](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy)

#### compromesso preliminary contract

Also: contratto preliminare

The preliminary contract that binds both sides to sign the deed later.

It normally comes with a deposit of 10% to 30% of the price, according to our Italy guide.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Italy](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy)

#### rogito the notary's deed

Also: atto notarile di compravendita

The final deed of sale, signed before a notary (notaio).

The notary checks the title and registers the sale. If you cannot travel you can sign through a power of attorney.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Italy](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy)

#### visura catastale cadastral extract

The extract of the cadastre for a property: its identification, class and cadastral income.

The tax agency states that the information in the cadastral and mortgage databases is public and open to everyone; only the floor plans (planimetrie) are reserved for people with rights over the property. Our Italy guide asks buyers to get the extract together with proof that the building matches its plans.

Sources: [Agenzia delle Entrate](https://www.agenziaentrate.gov.it/portale/schede/fabbricatiterreni/consultazione-personale/scheda-info-consultazione-personale-cittadini) · [RealHunt country file: Italy](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy)

#### conformità urbanistica e catastale planning and cadastral conformity

Proof that the building as it stands matches its permits and its cadastral plans.

Our Italy guide lists it among the checks before signing, next to the energy certificate and any unpaid debts on the property.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Italy](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy)

#### APE energy certificate

Also: attestato di prestazione energetica

The energy performance certificate of the home.

Ask for it with the other papers before you sign.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Italy](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy)

#### imposta di registro registration tax

The tax on buying from a private seller.

Our Italy guide gives 9% of the cadastral value for a second home, or 2% if the house becomes your main home, plus two fixed taxes of €50 each and the notary's fee.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Italy](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy)

#### IMU yearly council tax on second homes

Also: imposta municipale propria

The yearly municipal tax on second homes.

Our files give 0.4% to 1.06% of the cadastral value, plus the local waste tax (TARI). For small rural houses the two often add up to a few hundred euros a year.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Italy](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy)

Glossary · Japanese

## Buying a home in Japan: the local words, explained

Japan sells empty country houses for the price of a car, and the process has its own vocabulary: the explanation you must hear before signing, the scrivener who registers you and the person who receives your tax bills.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- akiya
- jūyō jikō setsumei
- tetsukekin
- shihō shoshi
- kotei shisan zei
- nōzei kanrinin
- chūkai tesūryō

#### akiya vacant house

Also: 空き家

A vacant house.

The 2023 Housing and Land Survey of the Statistics Bureau counted 9,002 thousand vacant dwellings out of 65,047 thousand, 13.8% of the stock, the highest share on record. For cheap vacant homes of up to ¥8 million, the agent's fee has a special cap of ¥330,000 including tax.

Sources: [Statistics Bureau of Japan](https://www.stat.go.jp/english/info/news/20241030.html) · [RealHunt country file: Japan](https://realhunt.co/costs/japan)

#### jūyō jikō setsumei explanation of important matters

Also: 重要事項説明

The explanation of the property's legal status that a licensed specialist must give the buyer before the contract.

It can be done by video call, which matters to anyone buying from abroad. Many cheap homes are advertised only in Japanese, so an agent who translates helps here.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Japan](https://realhunt.co/costs/japan)

#### tetsukekin deposit at the contract

Also: 手付金

The deposit paid when the sale contract is signed.

About 5% to 10% of the price. If you pull out after this point you lose it. The offer that comes before, the purchase application, is not binding.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Japan](https://realhunt.co/costs/japan)

#### shihō shoshi judicial scrivener

Also: 司法書士

The judicial scrivener, the professional who registers the transfer of ownership.

On settlement day you pay the balance and get the keys, and the scrivener registers the transfer at the Legal Affairs Bureau. The fee is about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000. Since 5 October 2026 every buyer must show proof of nationality when registering.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Japan](https://realhunt.co/costs/japan)

#### kotei shisan zei fixed asset tax

Also: 固定資産税

The yearly tax on land and buildings.

It is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, which is usually well below market value, plus a city planning tax (toshi keikaku zei) of up to 0.3% in urban areas. Small residential plots get a lower tax base.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Japan](https://realhunt.co/costs/japan)

#### nōzei kanrinin tax representative

Also: 納税管理人

A person with a Japanese address who receives and pays the tax bills of an owner who lives abroad.

A non-resident owner needs one. Non-residents must also report the purchase to the Bank of Japan within 20 days under the Foreign Exchange Act.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Japan](https://realhunt.co/costs/japan)

#### chūkai tesūryō agent's fee

Also: 仲介手数料

The estate agent's fee, paid by the buyer and capped by rule.

The cap is 3% of the price plus ¥60,000, plus 10% consumption tax. Other buying costs are registration tax (1.5% on land until March 2029 and 2% as the standard on the building), a real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value and stamp duty.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Japan](https://realhunt.co/costs/japan)

Glossary · Spanish and English

## Buying a home in Mexico and the United States: the local words, explained

On one side of the border a bank may have to hold the title for you; on the other, a company insures the title and a neutral account holds the money. The first six words are Mexican, the last six American.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- zona restringida
- fideicomiso
- ejido
- escritura pública
- ISAI
- predial
- buyer's agent agreement
- home inspection
- title insurance
- escrow
- HOA dues
- closing
- FIRPTA

#### zona restringida restricted zone

The strip within 50 km of the coast and 100 km of a border where foreigners cannot hold title directly.

It covers places such as Tulum and Playa del Carmen. Outside it you can own in your own name.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Mexico](https://realhunt.co/costs/mexico)

#### fideicomiso bank trust

A bank trust in which a Mexican bank holds the title for a foreign buyer in the restricted zone.

The alternative is a Mexican company. The foreign ministry (SRE) permit for a trust cost MXN 21,650 in 2026, and the bank charges a yearly fee of about US$450 to US$1,000.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Mexico](https://realhunt.co/costs/mexico)

#### ejido communal farm land

Communal agricultural land, which cannot be sold in the normal way.

Our Mexico guide tells buyers to confirm the land is not ejido when they check the seller's title, liens and disputes.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Mexico](https://realhunt.co/costs/mexico)

#### escritura pública public deed

Also: notario público

The public deed, prepared and signed by a public notary.

The notary registers it in the Public Registry. A separate buyer's lawyer is recommended for an independent review, and no deposit should be wired until the documents and the title have been reviewed.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Mexico](https://realhunt.co/costs/mexico)

#### ISAI acquisition tax

Also: impuesto sobre adquisición de inmuebles

The tax on acquiring property in Mexico.

Our Mexico file gives 2% to 5%, plus notary fees of 0.5% to 1% and legal fees of 1% to 1.5%, and 0.5% to 1.5% more for setting up the trust and its permit.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Mexico](https://realhunt.co/costs/mexico)

#### predial yearly property tax

Also: impuesto predial

The yearly local property tax in Mexico.

Usually 0.05% to 1.2% of the official cadastral value, which is often well below market value.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Mexico](https://realhunt.co/costs/mexico)

#### buyer's agent agreement written agreement with your agent

The written agreement a buyer signs with an agent before being shown homes in the United States.

It sets out how much the agent is paid and who pays. Since August 2024 the seller no longer has to pay the buyer's agent, so the buyer may pay unless the seller agrees to.

Source: [RealHunt country file: United States](https://realhunt.co/costs/united-states)

#### home inspection inspection of the house

An inspection of the condition of the house, often part of the buying process.

Our United States guide pairs it with a title search, so you know the condition of the house and that the title is clean before closing.

Sources: [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/mortgages/answers/key-terms/) · [RealHunt country file: United States](https://realhunt.co/costs/united-states)

#### title insurance insurance on the title

Insurance against problems with the title, such as someone with a legal claim on the home.

The consumer bureau explains that the lender's policy only protects the lender; to protect yourself you may want to buy an owner's policy. Title search and title insurance are part of the closing costs.

Sources: [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/mortgages/answers/key-terms/) · [RealHunt country file: United States](https://realhunt.co/costs/united-states)

#### escrow account held by a third party

An account set up by the mortgage lender to pay property taxes and home insurance out of your monthly payment.

If your loan has no such account, or you buy without a loan, you pay those bills yourself.

Source: [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/mortgages/answers/key-terms/)

#### HOA dues owners' association fees

Also: homeowners' association

The fees paid to the owners' association of a condo building or a planned community.

They vary widely and are usually paid separately from the mortgage. The consumer bureau warns that if you do not pay them you can face debt collection and even foreclosure.

Source: [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/mortgages/answers/key-terms/)

#### closing the day the sale completes

Also: closing costs

The meeting at which the balance and the closing costs are paid and the sale completes.

The deed is then recorded with the county. Closing costs vary by state and typically run 2% to 5% of the loan amount. There is no federal ban on foreigners buying homes, but about 30 states have added some limits.

Sources: [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/mortgages/answers/key-terms/) · [RealHunt country file: United States](https://realhunt.co/costs/united-states)

#### FIRPTA withholding when a foreigner sells

Also: Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act

The rule under which the buyer generally withholds 15% of the sale price when a foreign owner sells.

It does not apply when you buy, only when you later sell.

Source: [RealHunt country file: United States](https://realhunt.co/costs/united-states)

Glossary · Dutch

## Buying a home in the Netherlands: the local words, explained

Dutch listings end in two letters, k.k., and Dutch sales turn on a three-day right to change your mind. These are the words to know before you bid.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- kosten koper
- overdrachtsbelasting
- koopovereenkomst
- bedenktijd
- VvE
- Kadaster
- OZB
- BSN

#### kosten koper buyer's costs

Also: k.k.

A price marked k.k. means the buyer pays the transfer tax and the notary's transfer deed on top.

The Dutch government explains that existing homes are usually sold this way. Agent, survey and valuation costs, if you choose to have them, are also yours.

Source: [Rijksoverheid](https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/documenten/vraag-en-antwoord/huis-kopen/met-welke-kosten-krijg-ik-te-maken-als-ik-een-huis-koop)

#### overdrachtsbelasting transfer tax

The transfer tax on buying property.

The tax office lists the rates for 2026: 2% for a home the buyer will live in for a long time; 8% for a home that is not the buyer's main residence, such as a second home, a holiday home or a home to rent out; and 10.4% for other property such as land or business premises. Buyers aged 18 to 35 can get a one-off exemption if they meet the conditions.

Sources: [Belastingdienst](https://www.belastingdienst.nl/wps/wcm/connect/bldcontentnl/belastingdienst/prive/woning/overdrachtsbelasting/tarieven_overdrachtsbelasting/het_tarief_van_de_overdrachtbelasting) · [Rijksoverheid](https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/documenten/vraag-en-antwoord/huis-kopen/met-welke-kosten-krijg-ik-te-maken-als-ik-een-huis-koop) · [RealHunt country file: Netherlands](https://realhunt.co/costs/netherlands)

#### koopovereenkomst written purchase agreement

The written purchase agreement; only this, once signed, binds a private buyer.

A spoken or emailed acceptance does not bind you, according to our Netherlands guide. The standard agreement usually asks for 10% of the price, or a bank guarantee, paid to the notary.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Netherlands](https://realhunt.co/costs/netherlands)

#### bedenktijd three-day cooling-off period

Three days in which the buyer can cancel without a reason and without paying the seller anything.

The period starts the day after you receive the signed contract, and at least two of the three days must not be a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday. A longer period can be agreed; a shorter one cannot. It also applies to a holiday home, but not to bare land.

Source: [Rijksoverheid](https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/onderwerpen/huis-kopen/vraag-en-antwoord/hoeveel-bedenktijd-heb-ik-na-het-kopen-van-een-woning)

#### VvE owners' association

Also: vereniging van eigenaren

The owners' association of an apartment building.

Every flat owner pays its contribution, and the building's insurance is taken out jointly through it.

Sources: [Rijksoverheid](https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/documenten/vraag-en-antwoord/huis-kopen/met-welke-kosten-krijg-ik-te-maken-als-ik-een-huis-koop) · [RealHunt country file: Netherlands](https://realhunt.co/costs/netherlands)

#### Kadaster land registry

The national land registry.

A Dutch civil-law notary signs the transfer deed, and you become the owner when the deed is registered here.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Netherlands](https://realhunt.co/costs/netherlands)

#### OZB yearly municipal property tax

Also: onroerendezaakbelasting, WOZ-waarde

The yearly municipal property tax, charged on the official value of the home (the WOZ value).

Each municipality sets its own rate. Owners who do not live in the Netherlands also pay income tax in box 3, based on the value of the property.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Netherlands](https://realhunt.co/costs/netherlands)

#### BSN citizen service number

Also: burgerservicenummer

The citizen service number used for tax and official business.

Someone who does not live in the country registers in person, with a valid ID, at one of the 19 municipalities that keep the register of non-residents.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Netherlands](https://realhunt.co/costs/netherlands)

Glossary · Portuguese

## Buying a home in Portugal: the local words, explained

Portuguese paperwork is short on steps and long on acronyms. These are the ones on every purchase: the tax number, the promissory contract, the two property papers and the two taxes.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- NIF
- CPCV
- caderneta predial
- certidão permanente
- escritura
- IMT
- IMI

#### NIF tax number

Also: número de identificação fiscal

The Portuguese tax number, needed before anything is signed.

You get it at a tax office (Finanças) or through a representative. Buyers who live outside the EU usually need a fiscal representative.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Portugal](https://realhunt.co/costs/portugal)

#### CPCV promissory contract

Also: contrato-promessa de compra e venda

The promissory contract that fixes the price and the date of the deed.

It comes with a deposit of 10% to 30% of the price, according to our Portugal guide.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Portugal](https://realhunt.co/costs/portugal)

#### caderneta predial tax record of the property

The tax office's record of the property, with its tax value and whether it is urban or rustic.

Ask for it together with the permanent certificate and the habitation licence (licença de utilização) before you sign.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Portugal](https://realhunt.co/costs/portugal)

#### certidão permanente permanent land registry certificate

Also: certidão permanente do registo predial

The land registry certificate of a property, kept online and always up to date.

The justice portal says it is valid for six months, is always current and available over the internet, and has to be shown, for example, when you buy or sell a property. It tells you the owner and the debts registered against the house.

Sources: [Justiça.gov.pt](https://justica.gov.pt/Servicos/Pedir-certidao-permanente-de-registo-predial) · [RealHunt country file: Portugal](https://realhunt.co/costs/portugal)

#### escritura the deed

Also: Casa Pronta

The deed of sale, signed at a notary or at a Casa Pronta desk.

After signing, the sale is registered at the land registry office (Conservatória).

Source: [RealHunt country file: Portugal](https://realhunt.co/costs/portugal)

#### IMT transfer tax

Also: Imposto Municipal sobre as Transmissões Onerosas de Imóveis

The transfer tax on the purchase, on a sliding scale.

Our Portugal guide puts it at up to about 8% (5% on rustic land), plus stamp duty of 0.8%.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Portugal](https://realhunt.co/costs/portugal)

#### IMI yearly council property tax

Also: Imposto Municipal sobre Imóveis

The yearly municipal property tax.

Article 112 of the tax code sets the rates: 0.8% of the tax value for rustic property and from 0.3% to 0.45% for urban property, with each municipality choosing inside that band.

Sources: [Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira](https://info.portaldasfinancas.gov.pt/pt/informacao_fiscal/codigos_tributarios/cimi/Pages/cimi112.aspx) · [RealHunt country file: Portugal](https://realhunt.co/costs/portugal)

Glossary · Spanish

## Buying a home in Spain: the local words, explained

The words a Spanish estate agent, notary and town hall will use with you, from the first deposit to the yearly tax bill. Each one has a one-line meaning first, then what it means for a buyer from abroad.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- nota simple
- arras
- escritura
- NIE
- ITP
- IBI
- plusvalía municipal
- suelo rústico

#### nota simple Land Registry extract

A short extract from the Land Registry that identifies the property, who holds rights over it and what charges it carries.

The registrars describe it as informative only: it does not certify the entries, but it shows the owner or owners, mortgages, usufructs and other limits in force. It can be requested online from the registrars' own site, with an English translation if you ask for one. Our Spain guide lists it first among the checks on the house: it shows the owner and the debts.

Sources: [Colegio de Registradores de España](https://sede.registradores.org/site/propiedad?lang=es_ES) · [RealHunt country file: Spain](https://realhunt.co/costs/spain)

#### arras deposit contract

Also: contrato de arras

A private contract with a deposit that reserves the home before the deed is signed.

Article 1454 of the Civil Code says that when a deposit has been given, the sale can be undone by the buyer accepting to lose it or by the seller returning twice the amount. Our Spain guide puts the usual deposit at 10% of the price.

Sources: [Boletín Oficial del Estado](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1889-4763) · [RealHunt country file: Spain](https://realhunt.co/costs/spain)

#### escritura the deed of sale

Also: escritura pública de compraventa

The deed of sale, signed in front of a notary.

In Spain the deed is signed before a notario and then entered at the Land Registry (Registro de la Propiedad). The notary and registry bill is roughly €1,000 to €2,000 according to our Spain guide.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Spain](https://realhunt.co/costs/spain)

#### NIE foreigner identity number

Also: Número de Identidad de Extranjero

The identity and tax number Spain gives to foreigners.

You get it from a Spanish consulate or from a police station in Spain, and you need it to sign the deed and to pay taxes. Buying is open to foreigners on the same terms as Spaniards, but without this number nothing can be signed.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Spain](https://realhunt.co/costs/spain)

#### ITP transfer tax on resale homes

Also: Impuesto de Transmisiones Patrimoniales

The tax the buyer pays on a resale home, set by each region.

Our country files put it between 6% and 11% of the price depending on the region. A new build pays 10% IVA (VAT) plus 0.5% to 1.5% stamp duty (AJD) instead. It is the largest cost on top of the price, so check the rate of the region before you make an offer.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Spain](https://realhunt.co/costs/spain)

#### IBI yearly council property tax

Also: Impuesto sobre Bienes Inmuebles

The yearly property tax charged by the town hall.

The Local Treasuries Act sets the floor and the ceiling: from 0.4% to 1.10% of the cadastral value for urban property and from 0.3% to 0.90% for rural property; each town hall chooses its rate inside that band. Ask the seller for the last receipts: they show what you will pay and that nothing is owed.

Sources: [Boletín Oficial del Estado](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214) · [RealHunt country file: Spain](https://realhunt.co/costs/spain)

#### plusvalía municipal municipal tax on the rise in land value

Also: Impuesto sobre el Incremento de Valor de los Terrenos de Naturaleza Urbana

A municipal tax on the increase in value of urban land, which comes due when the property changes hands.

Article 104 of the Local Treasuries Act defines it as a direct tax on the rise in value of urban land shown when ownership is transferred. It is separate from the transfer tax the buyer pays and from the seller's income tax on the gain.

Source: [Boletín Oficial del Estado](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214)

#### suelo rústico rural land

Land classed as rural, where building is restricted.

For a country house our Spain guide tells buyers to check the status of the land and that every building on it is legal.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Spain](https://realhunt.co/costs/spain)

Glossary · Swedish and Danish

## Buying a home in Sweden and Denmark: the local words, explained

Two neighbours with opposite habits. In Sweden a bid binds nobody until the contract is signed and anyone can buy; in Denmark most buyers from abroad need a permit first. The first six words are Swedish, the last five Danish.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

- budgivning
- köpekontrakt
- lagfart
- pantbrev
- samordningsnummer
- kommunal fastighetsavgift
- tilladelse fra Civilstyrelsen
- sommerhus
- bank- og advokatforbehold
- skøde
- ejendomsværdiskat

#### budgivning bidding

The round of bids for a home in Sweden.

The estate agents' inspectorate states that bids are not binding and that bidding stays open until the contract is signed. The seller decides who gets to buy, not the agent, and the agent must pass every bid on to the seller. In open bidding the other bidders see each bid; in closed bidding everyone has a set time to hand in a bid, usually in writing.

Source: [Fastighetsmäklarinspektionen](https://fmi.se/vad-galler-vid-formedling/budgivning/)

#### köpekontrakt purchase contract

The purchase contract signed by buyer and seller in Sweden.

The seller's agent usually handles the paperwork. Until it is signed, nothing said during the bidding binds either side.

Sources: [RealHunt country file: Sweden](https://realhunt.co/costs/sweden) · [Fastighetsmäklarinspektionen](https://fmi.se/vad-galler-vid-formedling/budgivning/)

#### lagfart registration of title

The registration of the buyer as owner at Lantmäteriet, the Swedish land registry.

Lantmäteriet charges stamp duty of 1.5% for individuals (4.25% for companies) plus a processing fee of SEK 825. Our Sweden file adds that the duty is counted on the price or the tax value, whichever is higher, and that a cooperative flat (bostadsrätt) has no lagfart.

Sources: [Lantmäteriet](https://www2.lantmateriet.se/stamp-duty-and-fees) · [RealHunt country file: Sweden](https://realhunt.co/costs/sweden)

#### pantbrev mortgage deed

A mortgage deed on the property, needed if you borrow against it.

Taking out a new one costs stamp duty of 2% of the mortgage amount plus a fee of SEK 375 per deed.

Source: [Lantmäteriet](https://www2.lantmateriet.se/stamp-duty-and-fees)

#### samordningsnummer coordination number

The identity number Sweden gives to people who are not registered as living there.

You need it, or a Swedish personal identity number, to be registered as owner. You book an identity check at a service centre of the Swedish Tax Agency to get it.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Sweden](https://realhunt.co/costs/sweden)

#### kommunal fastighetsavgift yearly municipal property fee

The yearly municipal property fee on houses in Sweden.

SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Sweden](https://realhunt.co/costs/sweden)

#### tilladelse fra Civilstyrelsen permit to buy in Denmark

The permission that a buyer without Danish domicile, or without five years of past residence, needs to buy a home in Denmark.

It is given by the Department of Civil Affairs for a specific property. EU and EEA citizens who live and are registered in Denmark can buy a permanent home without it by signing a declaration to the Land Registration Court.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Denmark](https://realhunt.co/costs/denmark)

#### sommerhus holiday home

A Danish holiday home.

Buying one needs permission, and it is only given to people with particularly strong ties to Denmark, such as many years of holidays there. This is the rule that surprises most buyers from abroad.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Denmark](https://realhunt.co/costs/denmark)

#### bank- og advokatforbehold bank and lawyer approval clauses

Clauses that make a Danish purchase contract depend on the approval of your bank and your lawyer.

The seller's agent drafts the contract. Your own lawyer reviews it, the condition report, the title and the registered charges before the clauses are lifted.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Denmark](https://realhunt.co/costs/denmark)

#### skøde the deed and its registration

Also: tinglysning, tinglysningsafgift

The Danish deed; its digital registration (tinglysning) with the Land Registration Court makes you the legal owner.

The registration fee on the deed (tinglysningsafgift) is DKK 1,850 plus 0.6% of the price. If you borrow, registering the mortgage costs DKK 1,825 plus 1.25% of the loan.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Denmark](https://realhunt.co/costs/denmark)

#### ejendomsværdiskat yearly property value tax and land tax

Also: grundskyld

The two yearly property taxes in Denmark: one on the value of the home and one on the land.

Property value tax is 0.51% on 80% of the official valuation (1.4% above DKK 9.2 million). Municipal land tax (grundskyld) is set by each municipality and capped at 30 per mille of the land value.

Source: [RealHunt country file: Denmark](https://realhunt.co/costs/denmark)

## How to buy a home in Greece as a foreigner

The steps, papers and taxes, in plain words. General information, not legal advice: use a local lawyer before you sign.

### Can foreigners buy?

Yes. Buyers from outside the EU and EFTA need a permit to buy in designated border areas (parts of northern Greece and eastern Aegean islands such as the Dodecanese and Rhodes). The government has announced a 15% transfer tax for non-EU buyers of homes from 1 January 2027, not yet final in September 2026.

### The steps

- Get a Greek tax number: Apply for a tax number (AFM) with your passport. It is free and needed to sign contracts and pay taxes.
- Hire a lawyer: A lawyer is not mandatory but is strongly recommended. They can act for you under a power of attorney.
- Check the title: The lawyer checks ownership and searches the land registry for mortgages, liens and claims. Non-EU buyers in border areas apply for the permit at this stage.
- Sign a private agreement: Sign a preliminary purchase agreement and pay a deposit, usually 5-10%, which you normally lose if you withdraw.
- Pay the transfer tax: The notary prepares the transfer tax declaration and you pay the tax before the final deed.
- Sign the deed and register it: Sign the final contract before a notary and pay the balance, usually on the same day. The deed is then registered at the local land registry or cadastre.

### Costs on top of the price

About 5.5-7%: Transfer tax 3.09% of the price or the taxable value, whichever is higher; notary about 0.8-1% plus VAT; land registry fees about 0.5-0.7%; lawyer 1-2% plus VAT; if an agent is used, the buyer usually pays a commission of 1-3% plus VAT on top.

### Every year

Yearly costs are ENFIA and income tax on any rent.

Yearly property tax: Owners on 1 January pay the unified property tax (ENFIA), calculated per property from its location, size, age and official zone value, with an extra charge if total Greek property exceeds €500,000.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay Greek tax on Greek rental income at 15% up to €12,000, 25% to €24,000, 35% to €36,000 and 45% above, after a flat 5% deduction for expenses.

## How to buy a home in Italy as a foreigner

The steps, papers and taxes, in plain words. General information, not legal advice: use a local lawyer before you sign.

### Can foreigners buy?

Yes for EU citizens; non-EU buyers need reciprocity (US, UK, Canada, Australia qualify).

### The steps

- Get a codice fiscale: Your Italian tax code. It is free, from the Agenzia delle Entrate in Italy or an Italian consulate abroad.
- Make a written offer: The proposta d'acquisto usually comes with a small deposit. Once accepted, many buyers sign a preliminary contract (compromesso) with a 10–30% deposit.
- Check the house: Ask for the land registry extract (visura catastale), proof the building matches its plans (conformità urbanistica e catastale), the energy certificate (APE) and any unpaid debts on the property.
- Sign at the notary: The deed (rogito) is signed before a notaio, who checks the title and registers the sale. You can sign by power of attorney if you cannot travel.
- Pay the taxes: Buying from a private seller: registration tax 9% of the cadastral value for a second home, or 2% if it becomes your main home, plus €50 + €50 fixed taxes and the notary's fee.

### Costs on top of the price

About 4-15%: Registration tax 9% on a second home (resale), or VAT on new builds; notary 1-2% + legal ~1% + agent ~3% (GPG roundtrip 10-18%).

### Every year

IMU (council property tax) on second homes and a local waste tax (TARI). For small rural houses these are often a few hundred euros a year.

Yearly property tax: IMU 0.4-1.06% on second homes (on cadastral value).

Tax on rental income: Optional flat 'cedolare secca' on short lets: 21% for one property, 26% from the second.

## How to buy a home in Japan as a foreigner

The steps, papers and taxes, in plain words. General information, not legal advice: use a local lawyer before you sign.

### Can foreigners buy?

Yes. Foreigners can buy freehold land and homes on the same terms as Japanese citizens, even on a tourist visa, though buying does not give a visa or residency.

### The steps

- Find a home and agent: Any licensed agent can show you most listings. Many cheap homes are only advertised in Japanese, so an agent who translates helps.
- Submit a written offer: Send a non-binding purchase application with your price and conditions. Non-residents usually pay cash, since Japanese banks rarely lend to them.
- Hear the property explanation: Before the contract, a licensed specialist must explain the property's legal status. This can be done by video call.
- Sign and pay a deposit: Sign the sale contract and pay a deposit of about 5-10%. If you pull out after this, you lose the deposit.
- Pay and register: On settlement day you pay the balance and get the keys, and a judicial scrivener registers the transfer at the Legal Affairs Bureau. Since October 5, 2026 all buyers must show proof of nationality when registering.
- File reports and name a tax representative: Non-residents must report the purchase to the Bank of Japan within 20 days under the Foreign Exchange Act. You also need a tax representative with a Japanese address to receive and pay tax bills.

### Costs on top of the price

About 6-9%: The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.

### Every year

Expect fixed asset tax of 1.4% and city planning tax of up to 0.3% of assessed value, which is usually well below market value. Add the cost of a tax representative and, for apartments, monthly management and repair fund fees.

Yearly property tax: Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

Tax on rental income: Rent paid to a non-resident is subject to 20.42% withholding (except when an individual rents it as their own home), and the owner must file a tax return each year through a tax representative in Japan to settle the final tax.

## How to buy a home in Mexico as a foreigner

The steps, papers and taxes, in plain words. General information, not legal advice: use a local lawyer before you sign.

### Can foreigners buy?

Yes, but in the Restricted Zone (within 50 km of the coast or 100 km of borders, which covers Tulum and Playa del Carmen) only through a fideicomiso bank trust or a Mexican company; direct ownership elsewhere.

### The steps

- Check the restricted zone: Foreigners cannot hold title directly within 50 km of the coast or 100 km of a border. Outside that zone you can own in your own name.
- Choose how to hold title: In the restricted zone use a bank trust (fideicomiso), where a Mexican bank holds title for you, or a Mexican company. The foreign ministry (SRE) permit cost MXN 21,650 for a trust in 2026.
- Check the title: Verify the seller's title, check for liens and disputes, and confirm the land is not ejido land, which cannot be sold normally.
- Sign the purchase contract: Sign a contract that sets the price, payment terms and conditions. Do not wire a deposit until the documents and title have been reviewed.
- Close with a notary: A public notary prepares and signs the public deed (escritura). A separate buyer's lawyer is recommended for an independent review.
- Register the deed: The notary registers the deed in the Public Registry. Keep the final escritura and registration records.

### Costs on top of the price

About 3.5-8%: Acquisition tax 2-5% + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-1.5% (GPG 3.5-7.5%), plus 0.5-1.5% for fideicomiso/permit setup; TheLatinvestor budgets 5-8%.

### Every year

Yearly costs include the local property tax (predial), usually 0.05% to 1.2% of the official cadastral value, which is often well below market value. In the restricted zone add the bank trust fee, about US$450 to US$1,000 a year, plus HOA fees, insurance and upkeep.

Yearly property tax: Municipal predial, set locally on cadastral value; usually small, often less than HOA fees.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 25% ISR withholding on gross rent; plus 16% IVA on short-term stays (Airbnb remits on its bookings).

## How to buy a home in the Netherlands as a foreigner

The steps, papers and taxes, in plain words. General information, not legal advice: use a local lawyer before you sign.

### Can foreigners buy?

Yes. There are no nationality or residence rules and no surcharge for foreign buyers. Some cities, such as The Hague, restrict renting out cheaper homes after purchase without a permit (opkoopbescherming).

### The steps

- Get a BSN: Register in person at one of the 19 RNI municipalities with a valid ID to get a citizen service number (BSN).
- Set up payment and money: Open an account that can pay the notary on time and arrange financing.
- Make an offer: A verbal or email acceptance does not bind you; only a signed written purchase agreement (koopovereenkomst) does.
- Use the 3-day cooling-off period: A private buyer can cancel within three days of receiving the signed agreement without giving a reason.
- Pay the deposit: The standard agreement usually asks for 10% of the price, or a bank guarantee, paid to the notary.
- Sign the deed and register: A Dutch civil-law notary signs the transfer deed and you become owner when it is registered with the Kadaster.

### Costs on top of the price

About 2-9%: Transfer tax (overdrachtsbelasting) of 8% if you will not live in the home, such as a buy-to-let or holiday home, or 2% if it becomes your main home; a notary fee for the transfer deed of around EUR 500; Kadaster registration fees; and mortgage costs if you borrow; the seller pays its own agent.

### Every year

Expect municipal property tax (OZB), insurance and upkeep, and in a flat the owners' association (VvE) contribution. Non-residents also pay box 3 income tax based on the property's value.

Yearly property tax: Owners pay municipal property tax (onroerendezaakbelasting, OZB) on the official WOZ value, at a rate each municipality sets, which in practice is a per mille figure; tenants of homes do not pay it.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents declare Dutch property in box 3, where tax is 36% on a deemed return of 6% of the property's value in 2026, after a tax-free allowance of EUR 59,357 per person, regardless of actual rent.

## How to buy a home in Norway as a foreigner

The steps, papers and taxes, in plain words. General information, not legal advice: use a local lawyer before you sign.

### Can foreigners buy?

Yes. Anyone with the funds can buy property in Norway, and a built plot of up to 2 decares normally needs no concession (konsesjon) or self-declaration; owning property gives no right to live there.

### The steps

- Find a home and get loan approval: Search listings on Finn.no and get pre-approval if you need a mortgage; expect to put down 15 to 25%.
- Bid through the agent: Offers go through the seller's agent and bidding rounds can close within 24 hours, so inspect the home first.
- Sign the contract: The agent draws up the purchase contract; have a local lawyer review it.
- Pay at settlement: The price is paid through an escrow account at closing, and the deed is signed.
- Get a D-number if needed: Send Kartverket's D-number application with the deed and a certified passport copy no more than 3 months old.
- Register the deed: The deed (skjøte) is registered with Kartverket and the 2.5% document duty and fee are paid.

### Costs on top of the price

About 2.5-3%: Document duty (dokumentavgift) of 2.5% of market value, a registration fee (tinglysingsgebyr) of NOK 545 for the deed and NOK 545 for any mortgage document; a flat in a housing cooperative (borettslag) has no document duty; the seller normally pays the agent.

### Every year

Expect municipal property tax where it applies, municipal fees, insurance and upkeep. Costs such as municipal fees and property tax are deductible against rental income.

Yearly property tax: Some municipalities charge property tax (eiendomsskatt), at most 4 per mille of the value after a reduction of at least 30%, and some also give a basic deduction; many charge nothing.

Tax on rental income: Rental profit is normally taxed at 22%, and the Tax Administration says its rental rules also apply to owners who are tax resident abroad.

## How to buy a home in Poland as a foreigner

The steps, papers and taxes, in plain words. General information, not legal advice: use a local lawyer before you sign.

### Can foreigners buy?

EU, EEA and Swiss citizens buy on the same terms as Poles. Other foreigners can buy an apartment without a permit, but usually need a permit from the Ministry of the Interior (MSWiA) to buy a house or land.

### The steps

- Get a PESEL number: Apply for a Polish identification number (PESEL) in Poland, in person or through a lawyer with power of attorney. It is free and usually takes up to seven business days.
- Check if you need a permit: Non-EEA buyers of a house or land should apply for an MSWiA permit before buying. Apartments do not need one.
- Sign a preliminary agreement: Agree the price and pay a deposit, usually 10%. If you withdraw without cause the seller keeps it; if the seller withdraws they repay double.
- Do due diligence: A bilingual lawyer can check the land register (księga wieczysta) for liens, debts, unpaid fees and zoning issues.
- Sign the notarial deed: Sign the final deed (akt notarialny) before a notary and pay the fees. The notary files the change with the land register.
- Pay the PCC tax: Pay the 2% PCC within 14 days of the deed if the notary has not collected it.

### Costs on top of the price

About 2.5-4%: Tax on civil law transactions (PCC) 2% of the value, paid by the buyer within 14 days of the deed; notary fee (taksa notarialna) capped at PLN 1,010 plus 0.4% of the value above PLN 60,000, plus 23% VAT; court fee of PLN 200 to enter ownership in the land register (plus PLN 100 for a new register); optional lawyer about 1%; the agent fee (about 2-3%) depends on the agreement.

### Every year

Yearly costs are the local property tax, which is low for flats, plus income tax on any rent.

Yearly property tax: Owners pay a local property tax (podatek od nieruchomości) set by the commune, capped in 2026 at PLN 1.25 per m² of usable floor space for flats and houses.

Tax on rental income: Private rental income is taxed as a flat lump sum (ryczałt) of 8.5% of revenue up to PLN 100,000 a year and 12.5% above that.

## How to buy a home in Portugal as a foreigner

The steps, papers and taxes, in plain words. General information, not legal advice: use a local lawyer before you sign.

### Can foreigners buy?

Yes, same rights as Portuguese citizens (IMT increase for foreign second-home buyers announced Sept 2025).

### The steps

- Get a NIF: Your tax number, at a Finanças office or through a representative. Non-EU residents usually need a fiscal representative.
- Sign a promissory contract: The CPCV fixes price and date, with a deposit of 10–30%.
- Check the house: Ask for the caderneta predial and the certidão permanente (owner, debts, urban or rustic), and the habitation licence (licença de utilização).
- Sign the deed: At a notary or a Casa Pronta office, then the sale is registered at the Conservatória.
- Pay the taxes: IMT on a sliding scale up to about 8% (5% on rustic land) and stamp duty of 0.8%.

### Costs on top of the price

About 3-12%: IMT transfer tax 0-8% (progressive) + stamp duty 0.8% + notary/registry 0.9-1.2% + legal 1.25-2%.

### Every year

IMI (council tax), usually 0.3–0.45% of the tax value for urban property.

Yearly property tax: IMI 0.3-0.45% of taxable value (urban), set by municipality.

Tax on rental income: Long-term: 25% flat for non-residents; short-term (AL) under the simplified regime only 35-50% of gross is taxable.
