Question

## Can I buy a house without speaking the language?

Yes. Our country files list no language requirement for buyers, but the deed is drawn up in it, and the law protects you by requiring a translation. In Germany the notary must have the deed translated for a party who does not know enough German; in Spain an interpreter is required when the notary cannot explain the content personally; in Bulgaria a sworn translator signs with you.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

### Germany: the deed is translated instead of read aloud

Section 16 of the Notarial Recording Act deals with exactly this case. If a party, by their own statement or in the notary's judgement, does not know German well enough, the deed says so, and it must then be translated for that party instead of being read aloud. If the notary does not translate personally, an interpreter must be brought in, and an interpreter who is not generally sworn is to be sworn in by the notary unless everyone waives it. The interpreter also signs the deed.

Tell the notary's office when you book that you will need this, so the interpreter is there on the day.

Source: [Bundesministerium der Justiz](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/beurkg/__16.html)

### Spain: an interpreter when the notary cannot explain it

The Notarial Regulations say that when one of the parties does not know the language of the deed well enough, and the notary cannot communicate its content personally, an interpreter named by that party must take part. A notary who speaks your language can therefore explain the deed directly.

Before that day, the Land Registry extract (nota simple) can be ordered with an English translation from the registrars' own site.

Sources: [Boletín Oficial del Estado](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1944-6578) · [Colegio de Registradores de España](https://sede.registradores.org/site/propiedad?lang=es_ES)

### Bulgaria, Japan and Greece

- Bulgaria: the notarial deed is signed with a sworn translator if you do not speak Bulgarian.
- Japan: many cheap homes are advertised only in Japanese, so an agent who translates helps. The legal explanation that must come before the contract can be given by video call.
- Greece: a lawyer can act for you under a power of attorney, which moves the language problem from the signing table to one person you chose.

Sources: [RealHunt country file: Bulgaria](https://realhunt.co/costs/bulgaria) · [RealHunt country file: Japan](https://realhunt.co/costs/japan) · [RealHunt country file: Greece](https://realhunt.co/costs/greece)

### The contracts before the deed

The interpreter rules above apply at the notary. The papers you sign earlier, such as an offer or a deposit contract, are usually private documents with no such protection. Do not sign one you cannot read: ask for it in advance and have it translated by someone you pay. The [glossaries](https://realhunt.co/guide/glossary) explain the words you will find in them, country by country.

Question

## Do I need a lawyer to buy a house abroad? Notary or lawyer, country by country

A notary is not your lawyer. In Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Portugal and the Netherlands the sale is signed before a notary, but in Germany the notary is expressly neutral. A lawyer of your own is optional in most countries and strongly recommended in Greece, Denmark, Bulgaria and Mexico. Our files put the fee between about 0.5% and 2% of the price.

Reviewed on 14 November 2026 · Rules and figures as of November 2026 · General information, not legal or tax advice

### Countries where a notary signs the sale

- Germany: the law requires the contract to be recorded by a notary, who drafts it. The notary is neutral and does not act for you, so our guide suggests your own lawyer and a survey. Notary and land register fees are about 1.5% to 2%.
- France: the notary checks ownership, boundaries and rights of way and collects the compulsory surveys. The notary's own fee is about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; most of the bill is tax.
- Italy: the notary checks the title and registers the sale. Our file counts 1% to 2% for the notary and about 1% for legal help.
- Spain: the deed is signed before a notary and registered. Our file counts 0.5% to 1% for the notary and 1% to 2% for a lawyer.
- Portugal: the deed is signed at a notary or a Casa Pronta desk; our file counts 1.25% to 2% for legal help.
- The Netherlands: a civil-law notary signs the transfer deed, for a fee of around EUR 500.

Sources: [Bundesministerium der Justiz](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__311b.html) · [RealHunt country file: Germany](https://realhunt.co/costs/germany) · [RealHunt country file: France](https://realhunt.co/costs/france) · [RealHunt country file: Italy](https://realhunt.co/costs/italy) · [RealHunt country file: Spain](https://realhunt.co/costs/spain) · [RealHunt country file: Portugal](https://realhunt.co/costs/portugal) · [RealHunt country file: Netherlands](https://realhunt.co/costs/netherlands)

### Countries where a lawyer of your own does the checking

- Greece: a lawyer is not mandatory but is strongly recommended. The lawyer checks ownership, searches the registry for mortgages, liens and claims, and can act for you under a power of attorney. Fee: 1% to 2% plus VAT.
- Denmark: the seller's agent drafts the contract; your own lawyer reviews it and the papers before the approval clauses are lifted. About 1%.
- Bulgaria: a lawyer checks the title and the debts, which usually takes five to ten business days. Fee: 0.5% to 1%.
- Mexico: a public notary prepares the deed, and a separate buyer's lawyer is recommended for an independent review. Fee: 1% to 1.5%.
- England and Wales: there is no notary in a sale. The government's guidance says you can get legal advice or use a solicitor or conveyancer for the registration.

Sources: [RealHunt country file: Greece](https://realhunt.co/costs/greece) · [RealHunt country file: Denmark](https://realhunt.co/costs/denmark) · [RealHunt country file: Bulgaria](https://realhunt.co/costs/bulgaria) · [RealHunt country file: Mexico](https://realhunt.co/costs/mexico) · [GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/joint-property-ownership)

### Sweden and Japan: other professionals

- Sweden: the seller's agent usually handles the paperwork and legal advice is optional; you apply to Lantmäteriet yourself to be registered as owner.
- Japan: a licensed specialist explains the legal status of the property before the contract, and a judicial scrivener registers the transfer for about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.

Sources: [RealHunt country file: Sweden](https://realhunt.co/costs/sweden) · [RealHunt country file: Japan](https://realhunt.co/costs/japan)

### If you hire one

Choose a lawyer who is not recommended, paid or shared by the seller or the agent, agree the fee in writing before work starts, and ask what the fee does not cover. The percentages above come from our country files and are a guide for your budget, not a quote. Our [help buying](https://realhunt.co/help-buying) page explains the kinds of local help buyers use.

## Bali, Phuket, Tulum or Batumi? 400 new builds scored side by side

Median price, price per m², distance to the sea and facilities for 400 new-build projects. Batumi is the cheapest by far; Tulum is the furthest from the beach.

RealHunt Research · 2026-10-06

We keep a Top 100 of new-build projects in four places where foreigners buy holiday and rental homes: Bali, Phuket, Tulum and Batumi. This month we gave each of the 400 projects ten scores from 0 to 100. Here is what the four markets look like side by side.

Destination | Median price | Median €/m² | Under €100k | Median distance to sea | Within 1 km of sea | Ready now | Pool | Gym
[Batumi](https://realhunt.co/top/batumi) | €48,630 | €1,358 | 88 | 650 m | 73 | 34 | 56 | 44
[Bali](https://realhunt.co/top/bali) | €153,555 | €1,871 | 24 | 1.5 km | 41 | 64 | 93 | 64
[Tulum](https://realhunt.co/top/tulum) | €146,927 | €2,835 | 9 | 2.7 km | 6 | 1 | 98 | 13
[Phuket](https://realhunt.co/top/phuket) | €159,134 | €3,658 | 14 | 1.0 km | 50 | 45 | 94 | 59

Counts are out of 100 projects in each ranking.

### Cheapest: Batumi, by far

The median Batumi project starts at €48,630, about a third of the other three. 88 of its 100 projects start under €100,000, against 24 in Bali, 14 in Phuket and 9 in Tulum. Most are apartments in towers along the seafront, and 73 are within 1 km of the sea.

### Most expensive per m²: Phuket

Phuket's median is about €3,658 per m², almost double Bali (€1,871). In exchange, Phuket buildings list the most facilities after Bali: 94 have a pool and 59 a gym.

### Furthest from the beach: Tulum

The median Tulum project is 2.7 km from the sea in a straight line, and only 6 of 100 are within 1 km. Most new building is inland in La Veleta, Aldea Zama and Region 15. Tulum is also almost all off-plan: 1 of 100 is ready today, so the developer's track record matters more there than anywhere else.

### Best balance: Bali

Bali has 64 projects ready to move in, 41 within 1 km of the sea and the richest facilities: 93 pools, 64 gyms and 32 coworking spaces. Check the ownership: most foreigners buy leasehold there, and the listing does not always say which it is.

### Pick yours

Every ranking can be filtered and sorted by the ten scores: [Bali](https://realhunt.co/top/bali), [Phuket](https://realhunt.co/top/phuket), [Tulum](https://realhunt.co/top/tulum), [Batumi](https://realhunt.co/top/batumi). We wrote one article per destination too: [Bali](https://realhunt.co/blog/best-new-builds-bali-scored-2026), [Phuket](https://realhunt.co/blog/best-new-builds-phuket-scored-2026), [Tulum](https://realhunt.co/blog/best-new-builds-tulum-scored-2026) and [Batumi](https://realhunt.co/blog/best-new-builds-batumi-scored-2026).

### How the scores work

Every project gets ten scores from 0 to 100: price, value per m², location, beach, facilities, delivery, developer, space, visitor interest and listing detail. The grade of each project is the plain average of the ten. Price, value, space and visitor interest compare a project with the other 99 in the same ranking. Beach uses the straight-line distance to the coastline on OpenStreetMap, and facilities counts what the developer's public listing shows (pool, gym, spa, coworking, security and so on). Those two use the same scale in every destination, so you can compare Bali with Batumi.

None of this is advice to buy. Prices and dates come from public listings and change. Ask the developer before you decide, and check the facilities are built, not only drawn.

### How we pick

A person checks every home before it goes up, and homes that need major work, ruins, bare land and thin listings are turned down. The score then compares each home with every other home on RealHunt, from 70 to 98. Homes already listed in an earlier weekly Top 10 are left out.

Prices are the asking prices when each home was added. Homes sell, so check the listing before you travel.

None of this is advice to buy. Prices and dates come from public listings and change. Ask the developer before you decide, and check the facilities are built, not only drawn.

### How the scores work

Every project gets ten scores from 0 to 100: price, value per m², location, beach, facilities, delivery, developer, space, visitor interest and listing detail. The grade of each project is the plain average of the ten. Price, value, space and visitor interest compare a project with the other 99 in the same ranking. Beach uses the straight-line distance to the coastline on OpenStreetMap, and facilities counts what the developer's public listing shows (pool, gym, spa, coworking, security and so on). Those two use the same scale in every destination, so you can compare Bali with Batumi.

None of this is advice to buy. Prices and dates come from public listings and change. Ask the developer before you decide, and check the facilities are built, not only drawn.

## Not Every Cheap House in Japan Is an Abandoned Akiya

Stories about free houses in Japan usually show wrecks. These 18 homes start at €18,400 and you could move into them.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

You have probably seen the headlines: Japan has millions of empty houses, and some towns give them away. It is true. It is also why so many people are disappointed when they look closer. Most of the free and near-free houses need a new roof, new plumbing and months of work, and some are not worth saving.

So we set a different bar. The 18 Japanese homes on RealHunt all look like somewhere you could live now. Prices start at €18,400 and the middle of the list is €51,980.

[€54,280 · Hillside kominka with sea views over the Kyoto coastMaizuru, Kyoto, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/Da7vZIFDIuo)

### What the money buys

At the bottom of the range you get older wooden houses in the countryside: a 100-year-old farmhouse with its own farmland, or a 1977 single-storey house with a sakura garden in Usuki, Oita, about 500 metres from the sea. Around €40,000 to €60,000 the houses are often renovated, with new kitchens and bathrooms, and several have sea views on the Seto Inland Sea or the Sea of Japan coast.

[€19,320 · Japanese home with a sakura gardenUsuki, Oita, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DbbD15oDKLz)[€56,120 · Freshly renovated five-bedroom house with an ocean viewKashiwazaki, Niigata, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DcTSbXtj9qu)[€57,040 · Renovated island house with one of Japan's best sea viewsKojima, Okayama, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/Db59YYrjN5h)

At the top, around €91,000, there is a Japanese-style single-storey house with an engawa (the wooden veranda) and a garden in Yugawara, a coastal hot spring town about 90 minutes from Tokyo.

### Can a foreigner buy?

Yes. Japan lets foreigners own houses and land outright, with no visa or residency needed to buy. Buying costs add up to roughly 8% on top of the price: acquisition tax, registration, stamp duty and the agent's commission, which is capped by law. Owning a house does not give you a visa, so if you want to live there full time that is a separate question.

### What to check

Age matters in Japan in a way it does not in Europe. Houses built before June 1981 were built to older earthquake rules. Many are fine and some have been reinforced, but ask. Ask too about the septic system, whether the land is freehold or leased, and what the fixed asset tax is each year (usually low for older rural houses).

Distance is the other thing. A house in a quiet coastal town can be two or three hours from a big city by train. That is the point for some buyers and a problem for others.

## Cheap Houses in Sweden: What €22,000 to €99,000 Gets You

41 Swedish homes under €100,000, most of them red wooden houses on big plots near a lake. Where they are, what they cost to buy, and what to check.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

Sweden is the country people are most surprised by when they browse RealHunt. It has a reputation for being expensive, and in Stockholm it is. But 41 of the homes on our site are Swedish, all under €100,000, and most of them look like the picture you have in your head: a red wooden house with white corners, a garden, and a lake somewhere behind the trees.

### Where the cheap ones are

Värmland, in the west near the Norwegian border, has the most homes on our list. After that come Småland, Dalarna, Skåne and Jönköping. These are forest and lake regions with small towns, not suburbs. Many houses are an hour or so from an airport: Karlstad, Växjö, Jönköping or Göteborg depending on where you are.

The cheapest Swedish home on the site is €22,000, a wooden house in the forest 550 metres from a lake. The median is €72,000. For that you usually get a detached house with a plot measured in thousands of square metres, not hundreds. Several come with a sauna, a guest cabin or a barn.

[€22,000 · Charming wooden house in the forest near a lakeCentral Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dc6j54PF6hV)[€64,000 · Sea-view cabin with swimming access and boat mooringHornön, Västernorrland, Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdP0Csyilzz)

### How buying works

This is where Sweden is easy. Anyone can buy a house, whether or not you live in the EU. There is no notary. The buyer pays a stamp duty (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price plus a small fixed fee to register the title, and a mortgage registration fee if you borrow. The seller pays the estate agent. On a €60,000 house your buying costs are roughly €1,000 to €2,000.

Sales usually run as open bidding through the agent. The asking price is a starting point, and popular houses can go above it. You sign a contract, pay a deposit of around 10%, and the rest on the day you get the keys.

### What to check before you bid

Winter. Ask what heating the house has (wood, electric, a heat pump or geothermal) and what it cost to heat last winter. Several homes on our list mention geothermal or heat pumps, which bring the bills down a lot.

Water and drains. Country houses often have their own well and septic system. Ask when the septic tank was last emptied and whether the well water has been tested.

Access. A gravel road that is lovely in June can be hard work in January. Ask who clears the snow.

In Sweden the buyer is expected to inspect the house properly before buying, and hidden faults you could have found are usually your problem afterwards. Many sellers order an inspection report; read it, even with a translator, and consider your own.

## Why We Say No to Most Cheap Houses

A cheap house that needs €80,000 of work is not a cheap house. The rule we use to decide what goes on RealHunt, and why we turn most listings down.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

The internet is full of cheap houses. Most of them are cheap for a reason. The €1 houses in Italian villages come with an obligation to renovate, usually within three years, and the renovation costs far more than €1. The Japanese akiya you see in videos often need new roofs. And a lot of the American homes under $50,000 are listed for investors because they are not fit to live in.

RealHunt is for a different question: what can you buy for under €100,000 and live in, more or less as it is?

### The rule

Every home is looked at by a person before it goes up. We say no to:

- homes that clearly need major work: a new roof, rebuilt walls, no kitchen or bathroom
- ruins and shells, however pretty the stone
- land on its own, or land with a trailer or a shed
- listings with one photo, or photos of the town instead of the house
- anything over €100,000

Old is fine. Some of our favourite homes were built in the 1800s. What matters is that someone has looked after them.

In practice this means we turn down far more than we publish. We turn down about three listings for every one we publish.

[€75,000 · Fully renovated, fully furnished stone home in a quiet Tuscan villageSubbiano, Arezzo, Tuscany, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dc8Edq5j8H_)

### Where the homes come from

Some are found by our own research on public listing sites. Some come from people and accounts who post homes they have found, and every one goes through the same check. Signed-in members can open the original listing and contact the seller or agent directly. RealHunt is not an estate agent and does not sell the houses.

### How the ranking works

Every home that passes gets a grade from 70 to 98, built from 11 sub-scores: price, price per m², space, condition, extras, water, weather, airport, buying costs, listing detail and buyer interest. The front page, the country pages and the price lists are ordered by that grade, best first. Votes and saves only move the buyer-interest sub-score. [How the score works](https://realhunt.co/method). There are no paid placements in the ranking. Where there is a sponsored card, it says so.

### What we get wrong

Photos can flatter. Listings go out of date. A house that looks fine may have a problem only a survey will find. If you see a home that is sold or not what it seems, use the report button on its page and we will check it. And before you buy anything, anywhere, get an independent inspection and a local lawyer or notary.

## Italian Homes Near the Sea for Under €50,000: Where They Actually Are

Cheap Italian houses are usually in inland hill towns. A few are close to the water. Here is where they are and what the catch is.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

Most of the cheap Italian homes you see online are in inland villages, and there is a reason: the coast is where Italians go on holiday, so that is where prices are high. But not everywhere. On RealHunt right now there are a handful of homes under €50,000 that are on the coast or a few minutes' drive from a beach, and they cluster in three places: Calabria, Sicily and Puglia.

[€39,000 · Sea-view terrace in Acquappesa, CalabriaAcquappesa, Cosenza, Calabria, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/acquappesa-sea-view-39000)

### Calabria

The toe of Italy has the longest coastline of any mainland region and some of the lowest prices. In Acquappesa, on the Tyrrhenian side, there is a one-bedroom place with a sea-view terrace for €39,000, about 2 km from the water. Further south in Falconara Albanese there is a three-room flat with a sea view for €41,000. Two more homes in Calabria, at €30,000 and €35,000, are listed as five minutes from the beach.

[€41,000 · Apartment with sea view in Falconara Albanese, CosenzaFalconara Albanese, Cosenza, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/falconara-albanese-41000)[€30,000 · Sea-view house five minutes from the beachCalabria, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dcgta8yjCAR)[€35,000 · Sea-view house five minutes from the beachCalabria, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dc32k2tDKLf)

### Sicily

In Marsala, on the west coast, a 135 m² apartment is €34,000, about 600 metres from the sea. That is €252 per square metre, the lowest on the site for an Italian home with a size in the listing. In Acquedolci, on the north coast near Messina, a two-level flat that was largely renovated is €49,000. There is also a sea-view home with an 87 m² panoramic terrace 20 minutes from Messina for the same price.

[€49,000 · Duplex in Acquedolci, MessinaAcquedolci, Messina, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/acquedolci-49000)[€49,000 · Sea-view home with a panoramic terraceSicily, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dclv5CJDdhi)

### Puglia and Sardinia

Puglia has two whitewashed and vaulted houses around 20 to 25 minutes from the beach at €28,000 and €49,000. In Sardinia, a furnished tower house on four floors in a historic district is €35,000, about 3 km from the beaches.

### The catch

These are mostly apartments or small village houses, not villas. Sea views at this price usually come with stairs, a small kitchen and a building that has seen a few decades. Summer is busy and some coastal towns are very quiet from November to March. And the costs of buying in Italy are high: plan for 10% on top, plus about €2,500 in fees.

Always ask for the APE (the energy certificate) and whether the property is "conforme": that what is built matches what is registered at the land registry. A good local geometra can check this for a few hundred euros, and it is worth every one.

All of them in one place: [cheap houses by the sea in Italy](https://realhunt.co/cheap-houses/by-the-sea-in-italy). For the hill towns, see [stone houses in Italy](https://realhunt.co/cheap-houses/stone-houses-in-italy).

## How Many Months of Rent Would Buy You a Whole House?

We divided the median price of homes on RealHunt by three monthly rents. At €1,200 a month, a typical Italian village house costs less than three years of rent.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

This is the comparison that surprises people most. If you pay €1,200 a month in rent, you hand over €14,400 a year. In three years that is €43,200, which is more than the median price of an Italian home on our site (€41,000).

That does not mean you should quit your lease tomorrow. A house in a village two hours from the nearest city is not the same thing as a flat near your job. But the comparison is useful because it puts a price you cannot picture (a house in another country) next to one you pay every month.

### The table

We took the median price of the homes published on RealHunt in each country and divided it by three monthly rents: €800, €1,200 and €2,000. We did not use official rent figures for any city. Pick the column closest to what you pay.

Country | Median home on RealHunt | Months at €800 | Months at €1,200 | Months at €2,000
Italy | €41,000 | 51 | 34 | 20
Japan | €51,980 | 65 | 43 | 26
Sweden | €72,000 | 90 | 60 | 36
Mexico | €80,920 | 101 | 67 | 40
United States | €85,929 | 107 | 72 | 43
Canada | €92,552 | 116 | 77 | 46

Across all 140 homes the median is €61,280. At €1,200 a month that is 51 months of rent, a little over four years.

### What the table leaves out

Buying costs come first. They range from about 2% of the price in Sweden to about 10% in Italy, plus fixed fees. On each home page we show the estimate for that exact price.

Then there is the cost of keeping a house. Council tax on a small Italian village home is often a few hundred euros a year. In Sweden and Canada, heating in winter is the big one. In the US, property tax is set by the county and is usually shown in the listing. None of this is close to rent, but it is not zero.

And there is the part no spreadsheet captures: whether you actually want to live there. The cheapest homes are cheap because people left those places. Some are coming back to life with remote workers and retirees; others are quiet for a reason. Visit before you buy. Stay a week, in winter if you can.

### Try it with your own rent

On every home page on RealHunt there is a line that says how many months of rent the house is worth. It uses a rough average rent for the city your browser is in. It is a nudge, not financial advice, but it is a fair way to see these prices.

[€16,000 · Two-bedroom apartment with terrace in a historic Tuscan villageMontieri, Grosseto, Tuscany, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdSm-JkiJem)[€16,000 · Two-bedroom apartment with two balconies in a historic villageFiamignano, Rieti, Lazio, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dcsm9sZoDMp)[€19,320 · Japanese home with a sakura gardenUsuki, Oita, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DbbD15oDKLz)

## Move-In-Ready Houses in the US for Around $100,000

We published 13 US homes that cost under €100,000 and do not need gutting. They start at $75,000. Here is where they are.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

Search for cheap houses in the US and you find thousands under $100,000. Open them and many are the same story: fire damage, boarded windows, "cash only, investor special". We went through them looking for the opposite, homes you could move into this month, and published 13 so far.

They are asking between $75,000 and $110,000. On RealHunt every price is in euros so homes in different countries can be compared; at the rate we used, that is €65,428 to €95,961.

[€65,428 · Updated 3-bed townhouse in McKees Rocks, PennsylvaniaMcKees Rocks, Pennsylvania](https://realhunt.co/deal/mckees-rocks-65428)

### Where they are

The Pittsburgh area comes up more than anywhere else. McKees Rocks, McKeesport and Clairton, old steel towns along the rivers, have brick houses from the early 1900s with updated kitchens for $75,000 to $98,500. West Virginia has two: a three-bedroom on a double lot in Huntington for $89,900, and a two-bedroom with a newer metal roof in Chapmanville for $95,000. Then Indiana, Ohio, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Texas, New York, and one condo near the beach in Little River, South Carolina.

[€78,426 · Updated 3-bed house in Huntington, West VirginiaHuntington, West Virginia](https://realhunt.co/deal/huntington-78426)[€82,875 · Move-in ready 2-bed house in Chapmanville, West VirginiaChapmanville, West Virginia](https://realhunt.co/deal/chapmanville-82875)[€85,929 · Updated 3-bed house in Clairton, PennsylvaniaClairton, Pennsylvania](https://realhunt.co/deal/clairton-85929)

### What "move-in ready" means here

We only publish a US home if the photos show a kitchen and bathroom in working order, floors, walls and windows in good shape, and no sign of major damage. It is not an inspection. It is a first filter so you do not waste an afternoon on a house with a hole in the roof.

### Buying as a foreigner

Anyone can buy a house in the US. You do not need residency or a visa. Buyer closing costs are usually 2% to 5% of the price: title insurance, escrow and recording fees. Property tax is charged every year by the county or town, often somewhere between 0.5% and 2% of the assessed value, and the listing usually shows it. Owning a home does not give you the right to live in the US; that is a separate visa question.

### What to check

Get a home inspection. Ask about the age of the roof, the furnace and the water heater, which are the big bills in the first years. Check flood zone maps for houses near rivers. And look at the street on a map: in some of these towns, prices can change a lot from one block to the next.

See them all: [homes in the United States](https://realhunt.co/homes/united-states).

## How to spot a property scam when you buy a house abroad

The warning signs we see in cheap-house listings, and six checks that stop most scams before you send any money.

RealHunt Research · 2026-10-23

Cheap houses attract buyers from far away, and that is exactly what scammers count on: you cannot easily visit, you do not know the local rules, and a good price makes you want to move fast.

### Warning signs

- The price is far below every similar home in the same town, with no reason given (ruin, auction, shared ownership).

- The "owner" lives abroad, cannot show the house and asks you to pay a deposit to "reserve" it.

- You are asked to pay by bank transfer to a personal account, by crypto, or through a money-transfer service.

- The photos appear on other listings with a different address or price. A reverse image search takes a minute.

- Pressure: "three other buyers are interested", "the offer ends today".

- No land-registry or cadastral reference, or the seller refuses to give one.

### Six checks before you pay anything

- Get the registry extract. In Spain the nota simple, in Italy the visura catastale, in France the extrait cadastral. It shows who owns the house and whether there are debts on it.

- Check the owner's name matches the seller. If an agent sells, ask for the signed mandate from the owner.

- Use your own lawyer or notary, not one recommended by the seller.

- Pay only into an escrow or a notary's client account, never to a person.

- Visit, or send someone. A local surveyor or a video call walking through every room is enough to prove the house exists and matches the photos.

- Read the reservation contract before you sign: what happens to your deposit if the sale fails.

### What RealHunt does

A person checks every home before it goes up, and we link to the original listing so you deal with the real seller or agent. That is not a guarantee: if something on a listing looks wrong, use the report button on its page and we check it.

This is general information, not legal advice. Before you buy, get a local lawyer or notary.

RealHunt Research · 2026-11-07

Under $300,000 within half an hour of Miami sounds impossible, and most listings at that price are either far out, in rough blocks, sold "as is" or in old towers facing big repair bills. ### Where they are

Doral (two homes) is the business and family district west of Miami Airport, with good schools, CityPlace and big parks. Downtown Hollywood (two) is walkable, between Young Circle, Hollywood Boulevard and the beach, about 25 minutes from Miami. Pembroke Pines and Miramar (three, all on lakes) are quiet, green Broward suburbs with good schools, 30 minutes from Miami. Plantation (two) is leafy central Broward next to Fort Lauderdale. Kendall (one) is the established south-west Miami suburb, in a guard-gated community on a lake.

### What they really cost every month

In Florida the cheap price is only half the story, so every home page on RealHunt shows the monthly costs in large type:

- Community fee (HOA). Condos and townhouses pay one every month, often $400 to $900, sometimes including water, cable or building insurance. Two of these listings state it ($625 in Doral and $135 in Miramar); for the others we mark it as not stated, so ask the agent before you visit.

- Property tax. Florida resets the taxable value when a home sells. Listings show what the seller pays, often with a homestead discount; a new owner pays about 1.8% of the price, roughly $4,400 to $5,400 a year for these homes.

- Older condo buildings. Since 2022 Florida requires older condo buildings to pass structural inspections and keep repair reserves, which has led to large special assessments in some towers. We avoided any listing that mentioned one, but ask for the latest inspection, the reserve study and the board minutes before you make an offer.

- Insurance. Home insurance is extra. Impact windows, like those in the two Westview townhouses, lower it.

## What to check when you visit a cheap house: a 20-point checklist

Roof, damp, water, power, access, paperwork: the things that turn a cheap house into an expensive one, and how to check them in one visit.

RealHunt Research · 2026-10-23

Most cheap houses are cheap because of something you can see on a visit, if you know where to look. Take this list with you, or send it to the person who visits for you.

### Outside

- Roof: missing or slipped tiles, sagging lines, stains on the ceiling below.

- Walls: cracks wider than a coin, especially diagonal ones from window corners.

- Damp: a white salt line or flaking paint at the bottom of walls.

- Drainage: where rain water goes, and whether the ground slopes toward the house.

- Access: can a car or a van reach the door all year? Who owns the track?

- Boundaries: does the plot on the ground match the plot on the cadastral map?

### Inside

- Smell: a musty smell means damp, even if the walls were just painted.

- Electricity: age of the fuse box, earthing, whether the supply is connected or cut off.

- Water: mains, well or tank; pressure at the top tap; hot water.

- Waste water: mains sewer or septic tank, and whether the tank meets current rules.

- Heating: what kind, what it costs a winter, and whether the chimney works.

- Windows: single or double glazing, rot in wooden frames.

- Floors: soft spots, slopes, woodworm holes in beams.

- Kitchen and bathroom: usable now, or a full rebuild?

### Around

- Phone signal and internet: test it in the house, not in the village square.

- Noise: visit once on a weekday and once in the evening if you can.

- Neighbours: empty houses next door can mean damp or structural problems shared through walls.

- Services: nearest shop, doctor and pharmacy, and how long the drive is in winter.

### Paperwork

- The registry extract matches the house you saw: rooms, size, outbuildings. Unregistered extensions can be a problem when you sell.

- Energy certificate, and any pending local taxes or community fees.

If several of these need work, get a quote before you make an offer: it is your best argument for a lower price. RealHunt's [help buying](https://realhunt.co/help-buying) page lists local surveyors and lawyers.

## What €50,000 Buys in 2026: 140 Checked Homes, Country by Country

We sorted every home on RealHunt by price. 46 of 140 cost €50,000 or less, and almost all of them are in three countries.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

€50,000 is roughly what a new mid-size car costs, or a deposit on a flat in most European cities. We wanted to know what it buys if you spend it on a whole house instead, so we sorted every home currently published on RealHunt by price.

The short answer: 46 of the 140 homes on the site cost €50,000 or less. They are not spread evenly. 29 are in Italy, 9 in Japan and 6 in Sweden. France and Denmark have one each. Spain, the United States, Canada and Mexico have none under that line.

Every home here passed the same check: a person looked at the photos and the listing, and anything that needs a new roof, is a ruin, is only land or has a single photo was left out. So these are cheap homes you could sleep in, not projects.

### Italy: the most homes for the money

Italy has the cheapest home on the site, a stone house in a Lazio hill town for €12,000, about 55 minutes from Rome's Ciampino airport. Half of the 39 Italian homes cost €41,000 or less. At this price you are mostly buying in small inland villages: Tuscany, Lazio, Umbria and Abruzzo come up again and again. Expect thick stone walls, a small kitchen, and a piazza five minutes away on foot.

[€12,000 · Stone house in a hill town 55 min from RomeLazio, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/DcoUnwBDDxF)[€13,000 · Stone-village home near Viterbo, 1h30 from RomeGrotte Santo Stefano, Viterbo, Lazio, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/grotte-santo-stefano-13000)[€16,000 · Two-bedroom apartment with terrace in a historic Tuscan villageMontieri, Grosseto, Tuscany, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdSm-JkiJem)

What the price hides: Italy's buying costs are the highest on our list. For a second home, registration tax is 9% of the cadastral value (a tax value that is usually well below the price), and the notary and registry add about €2,500. Our cost estimate adds roughly 10% plus €2,500 to be safe, so a €30,000 house is closer to €35,500 all in.

### Japan: bigger houses, lower running costs

Japan's cheapest homes on RealHunt start at €18,400 and the middle of the list is €51,980. 9 of 18 are under €50,000. For that money the houses tend to be larger than in Italy, often with a garden, and many are near the coast in Wakayama, Kyoto prefecture and Okayama. Foreigners can own land and houses outright in Japan, with no residency needed to buy.

[€19,320 · Japanese home with a sakura gardenUsuki, Oita, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DbbD15oDKLz)[€34,960 · Single-storey Japanese house in a seaside townKainan, Wakayama, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdJ6Zs_DcnX)[€43,240 · Single-storey house with a huge lawn on the Seto Inland SeaMitoyo, Kagawa, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdWPFmBkdhr)

### Sweden: where €50,000 is the entry ticket

Sweden's median on our list is €72,000, higher than Italy or Japan, and only 6 of 41 Swedish homes are under €50,000. But what you get is often a detached wooden house with a big plot, near a lake, with a wood stove. Anyone can buy in Sweden, and the only real buying cost is a 1.5% stamp duty. There is no notary.

[€22,000 · Charming wooden house in the forest near a lakeCentral Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dc6j54PF6hV)[€25,960 · Cosy villa with sauna, 100 m from the riverNorthern Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdPBLT2CLlb)

### North America starts higher

In the United States the cheapest move-in-ready home we have published is €65,428 (a brick row house in McKees Rocks, Pennsylvania, asking $75,000). Canada starts at €55,842 and Mexico at €50,575. Those markets have plenty of cheaper listings, but at the very bottom many are sold as investor projects: boarded windows, fire damage, or a plot with a trailer on it. They do not pass our quality rule.

### What we take from this

If €50,000 is your hard ceiling, Italy is where you will have the most choice by far, Japan is where you get the most house, and Sweden is where you get the most land. Add 2% (Sweden) to 10% (Italy) on top for taxes and fees, and always pay for a survey before you sign.

You can see every home under €50,000 on one page: [houses for sale under €50,000](https://realhunt.co/cheap-houses/under-50000), or just [the ones under €30,000](https://realhunt.co/cheap-houses/under-30000).

Can foreigners buy? | Yes, buildings and apartments, with rights similar to locals; per GPG, foreigners can't own land directly, so a Bulgarian company is the usual route. | Without Danish domicile or 5 years of past residence you need permission from the Department of Civil Affairs (Civilstyrelsen); EU/EEA citizens who live and are registered in Denmark can buy a permanent home without permission by signing a declaration to the Land Registration Court. Tax on rental income | Non-residents pay income tax on Cyprus rental income at 20% to 35% after deducting 20% of the gross rent and loan interest, plus a 2.65% health contribution (GHS); the special defence contribution does not apply to them. | A non-resident who rents out a Danish home is taxed in Denmark on the profit under the ordinary Danish rules; staying in Denmark more than 3 months at a time or 180 days a year, or working there, makes you fully tax liable.

Tax on rental income | A non-resident who rents out a Danish home is taxed in Denmark on the profit under the ordinary Danish rules; staying in Denmark more than 3 months at a time or 180 days a year, or working there, makes you fully tax liable. | Non-residents: 25% ISR withholding on gross rent; plus 16% IVA on short-term stays (Airbnb remits on its bookings).

### How it is worked out

- Taxes and fees = price × the country's range. Both ends are shown, because the bill depends on the region, on whether the home is new or resale and on the lawyer.
- Each country page has three worked examples, what the costs are made of, the yearly taxes and the sources that were read.
- The same figures as a ranked table, with a CSV to download, are in [buying costs by country](https://realhunt.co/research/buying-costs-by-country).

### Sources

- Buying costs by country, with the sources of each one (RealHunt): [https://realhunt.co/research/buying-costs-by-country](https://realhunt.co/research/buying-costs-by-country)

Figures as of 2026. Rates and rules change: this is general information, not legal, tax or financial advice. Check with a local professional before you sign.

### Questions people ask

#### Which country has the lowest buying costs?

By the middle of the range, Georgia: 0.6 to 1.1% of the price. The highest is Northern Cyprus, with 12 to 22%.

#### Are buying costs paid in cash?

Almost always. Banks lend against the value of the home, not the taxes, so the buyer needs the costs in savings even with a mortgage.

#### What is not included?

Mortgage costs, currency exchange, furniture and repairs, and the costs of every year. For those, use the [running costs calculator](https://realhunt.co/tools/home-running-costs).

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: BPHTB transfer tax 5% + notary 1-2.5% + legal 0.5-1.5% (GPG: 6.5-9%); new developer units add 11% PPN/VAT (stack ~17-18% without the 2026 PPN-DTP incentive, ~6-9% with it). Plain leasehold deals mostly notary/legal.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: PBB land & building tax, up to ~0.5% of assessed NJOP-based value (low hundreds USD on a $300k villa).

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 20% withholding on gross rent (10% possible under a tax treaty); PT PMA companies 22% corporate tax.

## Buying costs in Canada: calculator and worked examples

Buying a home in Canada costs about 1.5 to 4% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €1,500 to €4,000, so €101,500 to €104,000 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Free calculator · General information, not advice · Figures as of 2026 · Sources

Taxes and fees (1.5 to 4%)€2,250 to €6,000

Total with the price€152,250 to €156,000

Canada: 1.5 to 4% of the price in transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and lawyer. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Put this calculator on your website
Paste this code where you want it to appear. It is free; the link to RealHunt under it is the only condition.

### Three worked examples for Canada

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
[€100,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/canada?p=100000) | €1,500 to €4,000 | €101,500 to €104,000
[€150,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/canada?p=150000) | €2,250 to €6,000 | €152,250 to €156,000

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 1.5% of the price and the high end 4%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Buyers usually pay provincial land transfer tax on a sliding scale (Ontario: 0.5% up to $55,000 and 1% from $55,000 to $250,000), legal fees of about $500 to $1,500, title insurance of about $250 and an inspection of $300 to $1,000, while the seller usually pays the agents; foreign buyers also pay Ontario's 25% non-resident speculation tax anywhere in Ontario and British Columbia's 20% additional tax in Metro Vancouver and four other regions.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Property tax is set by each city as a share of assessed value, from about 0.3% in Vancouver to 2.12% in Saint John in 2026.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents have 25% of gross rent withheld, but they can file a Section 216 return to pay tax on net rent instead, and Form NR6 lets the agent withhold on net rent.

### Questions people ask

#### How much are the taxes and fees on a €100,000 home in Canada?

About 1.5 to 4% of the price: €1,500 to €4,000, so €101,500 to €104,000 in total. On €150,000 it is €2,250 to €6,000.

#### What do I pay every year after buying in Canada?

Property tax is set by each city as a share of assessed value, from about 0.3% in Vancouver to 2.12% in Saint John in 2026. Add up your own bills with the [running costs calculator](https://realhunt.co/tools/home-running-costs).

#### Can a foreigner buy a home in Canada?

Mostly not for now: a federal ban stops non-Canadians from buying homes in cities and larger towns until January 1, 2027, with exceptions such as work permit holders and spouses of citizens or permanent residents. The ban does not cover rural areas and small towns, and the government has said it does not plan simply to extend it, but a replacement is being studied. See the rule for your nationality in [can I buy there?](https://realhunt.co/can-i-buy)

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Land Registry transfer fees of 3% up to €85,000, 5% to €170,000 and 8% above, halved for resales without VAT (1.5%, 2.5% and 4%); stamp duty abolished from 1 January 2026; lawyer about 1% plus VAT; small Land Registry charges.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.

- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: There is no annual national property tax (abolished in 2017); owners pay municipal fees of about €90 to €300 a year, plus sewerage and local authority charges.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay income tax on Cyprus rental income at 20% to 35% after deducting 20% of the gross rent and loan interest, plus a 2.65% health contribution (GHS); the special defence contribution does not apply to them.

## Buying costs in Denmark: calculator and worked examples

Buying a home in Denmark costs about 1.5 to 3% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €1,500 to €3,000, so €101,500 to €103,000 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Free calculator · General information, not advice · Figures as of 2026 · Sources

Taxes and fees (1.5 to 3%)€2,250 to €4,500

Total with the price€152,250 to €154,500

Denmark: 1.5 to 3% of the price in transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and lawyer. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Put this calculator on your website
Paste this code where you want it to appear. It is free; the link to RealHunt under it is the only condition.

### Three worked examples for Denmark

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
[€100,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/denmark?p=100000) | €1,500 to €3,000 | €101,500 to €103,000
[€150,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/denmark?p=150000) | €2,250 to €4,500 | €152,250 to €154,500
[€300,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/denmark?p=300000) | €4,500 to €9,000 | €304,500 to €309,000

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 1.5% of the price and the high end 3%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Registration fee on the deed (tinglysningsafgift) of DKK 1,850 plus 0.6% of the price, about 1% for a buyer's lawyer, and, if you borrow, a mortgage registration fee of DKK 1,825 plus 1.25% of the loan; the seller normally pays the agent.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property value tax (ejendomsværdiskat) of 0.51% on 80% of the official valuation (1.4% above DKK 9.2 million) plus municipal land tax (grundskyld) at a rate set by each municipality, capped at 30 per mille of the land value.

Tax on rental income: A non-resident who rents out a Danish home is taxed in Denmark on the profit under the ordinary Danish rules; staying in Denmark more than 3 months at a time or 180 days a year, or working there, makes you fully tax liable.

### Questions people ask

#### How much are the taxes and fees on a €100,000 home in Denmark?

About 1.5 to 3% of the price: €1,500 to €3,000, so €101,500 to €103,000 in total. On €150,000 it is €2,250 to €4,500.

#### What do I pay every year after buying in Denmark?

Owners pay property value tax (ejendomsværdiskat) of 0.51% on 80% of the official valuation (1.4% above DKK 9.2 million) plus municipal land tax (grundskyld) at a rate set by each municipality, capped at 30 per mille of the land value. #### Can a foreigner buy a home in Denmark?

Without Danish domicile or 5 years of past residence you need permission from the Department of Civil Affairs (Civilstyrelsen); EU/EEA citizens who live and are registered in Denmark can buy a permanent home without permission by signing a declaration to the Land Registration Court. Holiday homes (sommerhuse) need permission, which is only given to people with particularly strong ties to Denmark, such as many years of holidays there. See the rule for your nationality in [can I buy there?](https://realhunt.co/can-i-buy)

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: The buyer pays a 3% transfer tax (0% for qualifying first purchases under CONFOTUR tourism incentives), legal fees of about 1-2% and notary fees of about 0.25-1%, plus registration costs, while the seller pays the 2-3% agent fee.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: The yearly IPI tax is 1% of the part of a person's total Dominican property value, as assessed by the tax office DGII, above RD$10,695,494 in 2026, so a single cheap home is often below the threshold.

Tax on rental income: Rent paid abroad to a non-resident is generally subject to 27% withholding.

Buying a home in France costs about 7 to 8.5% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €7,000 to €8,500, so €107,000 to €108,500 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Taxes and fees (7 to 8.5%)€10,500 to €12,750

Total with the price€160,500 to €162,750

France: 7 to 8.5% of the price in transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and lawyer. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Put this calculator on your website
Paste this code where you want it to appear. It is free; the link to RealHunt under it is the only condition.

### Three worked examples for France

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
[€100,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/france?p=100000) | €7,000 to €8,500 | €107,000 to €108,500
[€150,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/france?p=150000) | €10,500 to €12,750 | €160,500 to €162,750
[€300,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/france?p=300000) | €21,000 to €25,500 | €321,000 to €325,500

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 7% of the price and the high end 8.5%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Transfer taxes (droits de mutation) of about 5.8%, or about 6.3% in departments that raised their rate for 2025 to March 2028; notary fee (émoluments) on a sliding scale from 3.87% down to 0.799% plus 20% VAT, about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; land security contribution (contribution de sécurité immobilière) 0.10%; disbursements (débours) of about €800 to €1,200; the agent fee is usually built into the advertised price (FAI) and paid by the seller, sometimes shared.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners pay an annual property tax (taxe foncière) set by the local authorities, and owners of a furnished second home also pay housing tax (taxe d'habitation), which some communes raise by a surcharge of 5% to 60%.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay French income tax on French rental income at a minimum rate of 20% (30% above about €27,500), plus social charges of 17.2%, or 7.5% for people covered by social security in another EU/EEA country or Switzerland.

Buying a home in Georgia costs about 0.6 to 1.1% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €600 to €1,100, so €100,600 to €101,100 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

### How it is worked out

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Only for tax residents: 0.05-1% of value depending on household income; non-residents generally exempt.

Tax on rental income: 5% of gross rent on residential property (long- or short-term), residents and non-residents alike.

## Buying costs in Germany: calculator and worked examples

Buying a home in Germany costs about 5 to 8.5% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €5,000 to €8,500, so €105,000 to €108,500 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Free calculator · General information, not advice · Figures as of 2026 · Sources

Taxes and fees (5 to 8.5%)€7,500 to €12,750

Total with the price€157,500 to €162,750

Germany: 5 to 8.5% of the price in transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and lawyer. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Put this calculator on your website
Paste this code where you want it to appear. It is free; the link to RealHunt under it is the only condition.

### Three worked examples for Germany

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
[€100,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/germany?p=100000) | €5,000 to €8,500 | €105,000 to €108,500
[€150,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/germany?p=150000) | €7,500 to €12,750 | €157,500 to €162,750
[€300,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/germany?p=300000) | €15,000 to €25,500 | €315,000 to €325,500

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 5% of the price and the high end 8.5%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) of 3.5% to 6.5% depending on the state (3.5% in Bavaria, 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein), plus notary and land registry fees (Notar- und Grundbuchkosten) of about 1.5-2%; if the seller hired the agent, the buyer pays half the commission by law, which is extra.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property tax (Grundsteuer), calculated since 2025 as assessed value x a tax rate x a municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) that each municipality sets.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident owners are taxed in Germany on net rental income at the normal progressive income tax rates, but without the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag).

## Buying costs in Greece: calculator and worked examples

Buying a home in Greece costs about 5.5 to 7% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €5,500 to €7,000, so €105,500 to €107,000 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Price | Taxes and fees | Total

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 5.5% of the price and the high end 7%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Transfer tax 3.09% of the price or the taxable value, whichever is higher; notary about 0.8-1% plus VAT; land registry fees about 0.5-0.7%; lawyer 1-2% plus VAT; if an agent is used, the buyer usually pays a commission of 1-3% plus VAT on top.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners on 1 January pay the unified property tax (ENFIA), calculated per property from its location, size, age and official zone value, with an extra charge if total Greek property exceeds €500,000.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay Greek tax on Greek rental income at 15% up to €12,000, 25% to €24,000, 35% to €36,000 and 45% above, after a flat 5% deduction for expenses.

## Buying costs in Japan: calculator and worked examples

Buying a home in Japan costs about 6 to 9% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €6,000 to €9,000, so €106,000 to €109,000 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Free calculator · General information, not advice · Figures as of 2026 · Sources

Taxes and fees (6 to 9%)€9,000 to €13,500

Total with the price€159,000 to €163,500

Japan: 6 to 9% of the price in transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and lawyer. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Put this calculator on your website
Paste this code where you want it to appear. It is free; the link to RealHunt under it is the only condition.

### Three worked examples for Japan

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
[€100,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/japan?p=100000) | €6,000 to €9,000 | €106,000 to €109,000
[€150,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/japan?p=150000) | €9,000 to €13,500 | €159,000 to €163,500
[€300,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/japan?p=300000) | €18,000 to €27,000 | €318,000 to €327,000

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 6% of the price and the high end 9%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

Tax on rental income: Rent paid to a non-resident is subject to 20.42% withholding (except when an individual rents it as their own home), and the owner must file a tax return each year through a tax representative in Japan to settle the final tax.

### Questions people ask

#### How much are the taxes and fees on a €100,000 home in Japan?

About 6 to 9% of the price: €6,000 to €9,000, so €106,000 to €109,000 in total. On €150,000 it is €9,000 to €13,500.

#### What do I pay every year after buying in Japan?

Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base. Add up your own bills with the [running costs calculator](https://realhunt.co/tools/home-running-costs).

#### Can a foreigner buy a home in Japan?

Yes. Foreigners can buy freehold land and homes on the same terms as Japanese citizens, even on a tourist visa, though buying does not give a visa or residency. See the rule for your nationality in [can I buy there?](https://realhunt.co/can-i-buy)

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 25% ISR withholding on gross rent; plus 16% IVA on short-term stays (Airbnb remits on its bookings).

## Buying costs in the Netherlands: calculator and worked examples

Buying a home in the Netherlands costs about 2 to 9% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €2,000 to €9,000, so €102,000 to €109,000 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Free calculator · General information, not advice · Figures as of 2026 · Sources

Taxes and fees (2 to 9%)€3,000 to €13,500

Total with the price€153,000 to €163,500

Netherlands: 2 to 9% of the price in transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and lawyer. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Put this calculator on your website
Paste this code where you want it to appear. It is free; the link to RealHunt under it is the only condition.

### Three worked examples for the Netherlands

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
[€100,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/netherlands?p=100000) | €2,000 to €9,000 | €102,000 to €109,000
[€150,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/netherlands?p=150000) | €3,000 to €13,500 | €153,000 to €163,500
[€300,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/netherlands?p=300000) | €6,000 to €27,000 | €306,000 to €327,000

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 2% of the price and the high end 9%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Transfer tax (overdrachtsbelasting) of 8% if you will not live in the home, such as a buy-to-let or holiday home, or 2% if it becomes your main home; a notary fee for the transfer deed of around EUR 500; Kadaster registration fees; and mortgage costs if you borrow; the seller pays its own agent.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners pay municipal property tax (onroerendezaakbelasting, OZB) on the official WOZ value, at a rate each municipality sets, which in practice is a per mille figure; tenants of homes do not pay it.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents declare Dutch property in box 3, where tax is 36% on a deemed return of 6% of the property's value in 2026, after a tax-free allowance of EUR 59,357 per person, regardless of actual rent.

### Questions people ask

#### How much are the taxes and fees on a €100,000 home in the Netherlands?

About 2 to 9% of the price: €2,000 to €9,000, so €102,000 to €109,000 in total. On €150,000 it is €3,000 to €13,500.

#### What do I pay every year after buying in the Netherlands?

Owners pay municipal property tax (onroerendezaakbelasting, OZB) on the official WOZ value, at a rate each municipality sets, which in practice is a per mille figure; tenants of homes do not pay it. Add up your own bills with the [running costs calculator](https://realhunt.co/tools/home-running-costs).

#### Can a foreigner buy a home in the Netherlands?

Yes. There are no nationality or residence rules and no surcharge for foreign buyers. Some cities, such as The Hague, restrict renting out cheaper homes after purchase without a permit (opkoopbescherming). See the rule for your nationality in [can I buy there?](https://realhunt.co/can-i-buy)

## Buying costs in Northern Cyprus: calculator and worked examples

Buying a home in Northern Cyprus costs about 12 to 22% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €12,000 to €22,000, so €112,000 to €122,000 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Free calculator · General information, not advice · Figures as of 2026 · Sources

Taxes and fees (12 to 22%)€18,000 to €33,000

Total with the price€168,000 to €183,000

Northern Cyprus: 12 to 22% of the price in transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and lawyer. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Put this calculator on your website
Paste this code where you want it to appear. It is free; the link to RealHunt under it is the only condition.

### Three worked examples for Northern Cyprus

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
[€100,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/northern-cyprus?p=100000) | €12,000 to €22,000 | €112,000 to €122,000
[€150,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/northern-cyprus?p=150000) | €18,000 to €33,000 | €168,000 to €183,000
[€300,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/northern-cyprus?p=300000) | €36,000 to €66,000 | €336,000 to €366,000

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 12% of the price and the high end 22%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Title deed transfer fee for foreigners 6-12% (sources disagree: 9% most cited, 12% in one 2026 guide) + 5% VAT on new builds (one source says 19%) + 0.5% stamp duty + legal GBP 1,000-2,500 + transformer fee GBP 1,500-3,000 on new builds.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Per m2, very low: about GBP 10-100/yr for a typical apartment or villa.

Tax on rental income: 10% of gross rental income (Investra, 2026).

## Buying costs in Norway: calculator and worked examples

Buying a home in Norway costs about 2.5 to 3% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €2,500 to €3,000, so €102,500 to €103,000 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Free calculator · General information, not advice · Figures as of 2026 · Sources

Taxes and fees (2.5 to 3%)€3,750 to €4,500

Total with the price€153,750 to €154,500

Norway: 2.5 to 3% of the price in transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and lawyer. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Put this calculator on your website
Paste this code where you want it to appear. It is free; the link to RealHunt under it is the only condition.

### Three worked examples for Norway

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
[€100,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/norway?p=100000) | €2,500 to €3,000 | €102,500 to €103,000
[€150,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/norway?p=150000) | €3,750 to €4,500 | €153,750 to €154,500
[€300,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/norway?p=300000) | €7,500 to €9,000 | €307,500 to €309,000

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 2.5% of the price and the high end 3%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Document duty (dokumentavgift) of 2.5% of market value, a registration fee (tinglysingsgebyr) of NOK 545 for the deed and NOK 545 for any mortgage document; a flat in a housing cooperative (borettslag) has no document duty; the seller normally pays the agent.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Some municipalities charge property tax (eiendomsskatt), at most 4 per mille of the value after a reduction of at least 30%, and some also give a basic deduction; many charge nothing.

Tax on rental income: Rental profit is normally taxed at 22%, and the Tax Administration says its rental rules also apply to owners who are tax resident abroad.

### Questions people ask

#### How much are the taxes and fees on a €100,000 home in Norway?

About 2.5 to 3% of the price: €2,500 to €3,000, so €102,500 to €103,000 in total. On €150,000 it is €3,750 to €4,500.

#### What do I pay every year after buying in Norway?

## Buying costs in Poland: calculator and worked examples

Buying a home in Poland costs about 2.5 to 4% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €2,500 to €4,000, so €102,500 to €104,000 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Free calculator · General information, not advice · Figures as of 2026 · Sources

Taxes and fees (2.5 to 4%)€3,750 to €6,000

Total with the price€153,750 to €156,000

Poland: 2.5 to 4% of the price in transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and lawyer. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Put this calculator on your website
Paste this code where you want it to appear. It is free; the link to RealHunt under it is the only condition.

### Three worked examples for Poland

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
[€100,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/poland?p=100000) | €2,500 to €4,000 | €102,500 to €104,000
[€150,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/poland?p=150000) | €3,750 to €6,000 | €153,750 to €156,000
[€300,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/poland?p=300000) | €7,500 to €12,000 | €307,500 to €312,000

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 2.5% of the price and the high end 4%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Tax on civil law transactions (PCC) 2% of the value, paid by the buyer within 14 days of the deed; notary fee (taksa notarialna) capped at PLN 1,010 plus 0.4% of the value above PLN 60,000, plus 23% VAT; court fee of PLN 200 to enter ownership in the land register (plus PLN 100 for a new register); optional lawyer about 1%; the agent fee (about 2-3%) depends on the agreement.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners pay a local property tax (podatek od nieruchomości) set by the commune, capped in 2026 at PLN 1.25 per m² of usable floor space for flats and houses.

Tax on rental income: Private rental income is taxed as a flat lump sum (ryczałt) of 8.5% of revenue up to PLN 100,000 a year and 12.5% above that.

- Where the money goes: New build: 10% IVA + 0.5-1.5% AJD stamp duty + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-2%; resale: ITP transfer tax 6-11% instead of IVA/AJD.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: IBI 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value (municipal), plus imputed income tax on unlet homes.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: EU/EEA 19% on net income; non-EU 24% on gross with no deductions.

### Questions people ask

#### How much are the taxes and fees on a €100,000 home in Spain?

About 7.5 to 14% of the price: €7,500 to €14,000, so €107,500 to €114,000 in total. On €150,000 it is €11,250 to €21,000.

#### What do I pay every year after buying in Spain?

IBI 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value (municipal), plus imputed income tax on unlet homes. Add up your own bills with the [running costs calculator](https://realhunt.co/tools/home-running-costs).

#### Can a foreigner buy a home in Spain?

Yes, no restrictions at present; the government has proposed a 100% tax on (or ban for) non-EU non-resident buyers, not enacted. See the rule for your nationality in [can I buy there?](https://realhunt.co/can-i-buy)

## Buying costs in Sweden: calculator and worked examples

Buying a home in Sweden costs about 1.5 to 3.5% of the price in taxes and fees. On a €100,000 home that is €1,500 to €3,500, so €101,500 to €103,500 in total. Type your own price: the result has its own link, to send to whoever is buying with you.

Free calculator · General information, not advice · Figures as of 2026 · Sources

Taxes and fees (1.5 to 3.5%)€2,250 to €5,250

Total with the price€152,250 to €155,250

Sweden: 1.5 to 3.5% of the price in transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and lawyer. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Put this calculator on your website
Paste this code where you want it to appear. It is free; the link to RealHunt under it is the only condition.

### Three worked examples for Sweden

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
[€100,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/sweden?p=100000) | €1,500 to €3,500 | €101,500 to €103,500
[€150,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/sweden?p=150000) | €2,250 to €5,250 | €152,250 to €155,250
[€300,000](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/sweden?p=300000) | €4,500 to €10,500 | €304,500 to €310,500

Each price opens the calculator with that figure. The low end of each range is 1.5% of the price and the high end 3.5%.

### How it is worked out

- Where the money goes: Stamp duty on the title (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price or tax value, whichever is higher, plus a SEK 825 fee; if you borrow and need new mortgage deeds (pantbrev), 2% of their amount plus a SEK 375 fee; optional legal advice; the seller normally pays the agent, and a cooperative flat (bostadsrätt) has no lagfart.
- Taxes and fees = price × the range above. They are a share of the price, so the sum works in any currency; the currency box only changes the symbol.
- The range covers new and resale homes and different regions. A cheap home is usually nearer the high end, because several fees have a minimum.
- Comparing with another country? Put two homes side by side in [compare the total cost of two homes](https://realhunt.co/tools/compare-buying-costs).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Houses pay a municipal property fee (kommunal fastighetsavgift) of SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident individuals pay 30% tax on net rental income as capital income; for a private home you can first deduct SEK 40,000 per property and 20% of the rent (the 20% does not apply to a bostadsrätt).
